Title: Damage assessment, repairs underway after Seberang Jaya Hospital ceiling leaks
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Damage assessments and repair work are underway at Seberang Jaya Hospital after torrential rain caused ceiling leaks in two blocks on Saturday.
The Penang Health Department said the hospital's engineering unit and building management concessionaire were conducting a comprehensive assessment and taking steps to contain the damage.
It assured the public that healthcare services remained unaffected, adding that no patients or medical equipment were endangered.
"Hospital personnel took prompt and appropriate action to manage affected patients and safeguard medical equipment at the relevant locations," it said in a Facebook statement.
The leaks followed an
unusually heavy thunderstorm
accompanied by strong winds between 5.45pm and 7pm, which caused rainwater to overflow at several locations in Block A (the old block) and Block B (the new block).
Most of the affected areas were in the older block.
The department said the Defects Liability Period for Block B ended on April 12 this year, with no unusual rainwater overflow reported during the warranty period.
Meanwhile, Permatang Pauh member of parliament Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan called on the Health Ministry to take immediate action, warning against waiting for a tragedy before addressing the problem.
He said the incident should not be dismissed as a weather-related issue and called for a comprehensive technical audit of the hospital's structural integrity, roofing and maintenance standards.
"The public deserves to know how such an incident could happen, particularly at a newly completed facility.
"The ministry must also provide clear details on the maintenance allocations and account for the parties tasked with keeping these facilities in optimal condition," he said.
Fawwaz also called on the Health Minister to explain the root cause and outline remedial measures, saying the safety of patients, healthcare staff and visitors must remain the priority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: Malaysia considers accelerating quantum migration to boost data security
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia is considering accelerating its quantum migration process to strengthen national data security amid advances in quantum computing technology that are expected to pose new challenges to cybersecurity systems.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had asked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to hold discussions with the National Security Council, the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and telecommunications companies to explore potential collaboration in this area.
He said the collaboration would involve establishing a research and development space to facilitate faster and more secure quantum migration in Malaysia.
He said this when commenting on technological innovations that could benefit Malaysia after visiting several exhibition booths at the Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026 here yesterday.
Fahmi said one of the technological innovations that caught his attention was quantum-safe communication, which is becoming increasingly important for future data protection.
He said the emergence of quantum computers on the market was expected to pose significant challenges to existing cryptography and encryption methods used to safeguard data.
"I foresee that quantum migration and quantum-safe communication will be among the key issues facing many countries in the years ahead.
"Quantum computers are expected to enter the market in the near future, posing major challenges to existing cryptography and encryption methods used to ensure our data remains secure," he said.
Apart from quantum technology, Fahmi said his visit to the exhibition booths also provided an opportunity to explore various innovations, including the integration of artificial intelligence into smart city services and security systems.
Quantum migration refers to the process of upgrading existing digital security systems to adopt quantum-resistant encryption technologies designed to protect data against potential threats from future quantum computers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flood victim numbers rise in Perak, fall in Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood victims in Perak recorded a slight increase while the situation in Selangor continued to show a downward trend, with a total of 654 people still sheltering at temporary relief centres (PPS) as of this morning.
The situation in Hilir Perak saw the number of victims increase to 439 people from 130 families this morning, compared with 414 people from 123 families yesterday evening.
The state Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said 277 victims from 84 families were housed at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall PPS, while another 136 people from 39 families were taking shelter at the MPTI Langkap Hall.
Meanwhile, 26 victims from seven families remained at the Manjung Community Hall PPS, comprising residents of Pekan Beruas, Taman Beruas, Taman Desa, Perumahan Awam, Taman Seri Delima, Taman Limau Emas, Taman Anggerik, Kampung Kilang, Kampung Dendang and Kampung Paya Lima.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast rain and thunderstorms in all districts in Perak this afternoon and tonight.
In addition, water levels in two rivers were reported to have exceeded the danger level, namely Sungai Kinta in Tanjung Tualang at 13.78m and Sungai Bidor in Changkat Jong at 3.53m.
In Selangor, the situation improved, with the number of victims at PPS decreasing to 215 people from 55 families as of 8am today, compared with 507 people from 143 families yesterday.
According to the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, two PPS were operating in Kuala Selangor, namely SK Parit Mahang, which housed 100 people from 23 families, and SK Jaya Setia (68 victims, 20 families), while SK Dato' Maharaja Lela remained activated despite having no occupants recorded.
In Shah Alam, 47 victims from 11 families were reported to be taking shelter at the Dewan Siantan Kampung Melayu Subang, Section U6 PPS.
Meanwhile, the Drainage and Irrigation Department's National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre, in a statement last night, said nine districts in Kelantan were expected to be affected by floods, namely Kota Baru, Tumpat, Bachok, Machang, Pasir Mas, Pasir Puteh, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Jeli.
The centre also forecast that several areas in Pahang, namely Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, could be affected by floods from yesterday until Wednesday, particularly in high-risk locations and low-lying areas.
In Terengganu, a similar alert was issued for six districts, namely Setiu, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Besut, Hulu Terengganu and Marang.

Title: Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Sabah under rain alert until Wednesday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy and persistent rain is expected in parts of Kelantan and Terengganu until Wednesday, with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issuing a severe continuous rain warning.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Bachok, Kota Baru, Tumpat, Pasir Mas and Pasir Puteh, while in Terengganu it affects Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus.
MetMalaysia has also issued a continuous rain alert for several areas in Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Sabah over the same period.
The affected areas in Kelantan are Tanah Merah, Machang, Kuala Krai and Jeli, while in Terengganu the alert covers Hulu Terengganu.
In Pahang, it covers Kuantan, Pekan, Rompin and Jerantut, while in Sabah the affected areas are Kudat, Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan.
The warning was issued at 8.30am today.

Title: Johari: Reliance on foreign workers must be reduced
Article:
AYER KEROH: Malaysia must reduce its dependence on foreign labour in phases by expanding the adoption of automation, robotics and digital technology, particularly within the manufacturing sector.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said this approach is crucial to ensure the sustainability of domestic industry without remaining perpetually reliant on foreign workers to meet operational needs.
"Our country already has 2.6 million foreign workers, and under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), we must control this figure gradually.
"We cannot rely on foreign workers for everything. We need to identify mechanisms that allow businesses in Malaysia to operate without being completely dependent on foreign labour," he told reporters after attending a dialogue session with the business community in Melaka yesterday.
Johari said foreign labour is still required for roles categorised as 3D — dirty, difficult and dangerous — but industry must transition towards a more sustainable business model.
He said prolonged reliance on foreign labour is not a viable long-term solution, as experienced personnel must eventually return to their home countries, compelling employers to train new recruits from scratch.
He added that the manufacturing sector in particular needs to ramp up the adoption of technology, including artificial intelligence, robotics and automation, to create higher-skilled jobs.
Such a shift, he said, is also vital to provide more suitable career opportunities for educated and skilled local talent.
"I understand this is not easy, as our culture of dependency on foreign labour has been deeply entrenched for a very long time.
"Therefore, this transition is not something that can be achieved in a year or two. It requires time," he said.
Meanwhile, Johari said the local workforce, including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduates, must be granted more opportunities to gain practical experience and master industry skills.
He added that there was a need to explore ways to retain the expertise of experienced foreign workers in manufacturing, whilst simultaneously intensifying training for local staff to enable them to take over those roles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MITI to consult Customs, MOF over machinery import duty issue
Article:
AYER KEROH: The issue of machinery import duties allegedly being imposed on local companies despite them securing exemption approvals from the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) will be raised with the Customs Department and the Finance Ministry (MoF).
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the matter was raised by several industry operators during a dialogue session with the business community in Melaka yesterday.
He said some companies claimed they were forced to pay duties upon despite already possessing exemption approval letters from Mida.
He said there were allegations that such payments could not be refunded even after the exemption status was subsequently clarified.
"This should not be happening. There are several cases like this, and I will be taking this matter up with Customs and MoF.
"If this continues, Mida becomes redundant. Companies come and apply, Mida grants the exemption, yet when the machinery is brought in, they are still made to pay duties," he said.
Johari said such circumstances could adversely affect the cash flow of local companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) investing to enhance production efficiency.
"They decided to purchase machinery to improve production efficiency. That is precisely why we grant the exemption.
"I have not yet had the opportunity to examine the documents regarding the issues raised in earlier dialogue.
"However, provide me with the facts and complete details, and I will look into it. If the payments have not been refunded, we need to ask why. For how long will people respect Mida if situations like this occur?"
Johari said it was important that government agencies coordinate matters to ensure that every policy introduced is implemented effectively across all levels of enforcement.
He said dialogue sessions with the business community are vital for identifying policy implementation issues and gathering direct feedback from industry operators.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Merz picks Ilse Aigner to become Germany's first woman president
Article:
BERLIN: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Sunday he intended to appoint Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as the country's next president, in 2027, making her the first woman in the post.
He made his announcement at a dinner for leaders of his centre-right CDU party, confirming information leaked last week by party sources.
Aigner, 61, belongs to the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of the CDU.
Aigner's nomination by Merz virtually guarantees her election on Jan 30, as those voting are almost all drawn from Germany's two parliamentary chambers.
Currently speaker of the southern state's regional assembly, she would replace outgoing President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a Social Democrat, in the largely ceremonial post.
Steinmeier, who took office in 2017, will reach the limit of two five-year terms in March 2027.
German political practice is that coalition parties agree on a common candidate for the job. The president is meant to be above party politics, representing the moral conscience of the country.
The current ruling coalition is made up of the CDU, the CSU and the Social Democrats of the SPD.
- 'PERFECT CANDIDATE' -
The SPD has frequently voiced its support for Aigner as president.
During the chancellorship of Angela Merkel, she served as agriculture minister, winning the respect of politicians outside her own party.
Dietmar Woidke, one regional SPD leader, told the news website Politico that she would be the "perfect candidate" for the job.
"She knows German politics like the back of her hand," he said. "She's accessible. She likes people, knows how to listen and people listen to her," he added.
Her appearances in traditional dress at Germany's beer festivals have also helped raise her profile in Bavaria.
And her way of dealing with the far-right AfD party in the Bavarian regional parliament is admired for being both firm and courteous.
At a time of increased political polarisation, and as the anti-migrant, pro-Russian AfD is registering a record 28 per cent in opinion polls, her admirers see her as a potential calming influence.
Aigner was born in Bavaria to parents who ran an electricity company. She survived a brush with cancer in her youth, when a tumour had to be removed from her back.
After technical studies, she worked as an electronics technician with a helicopter builder before moving into local and then federal politics.--AFP

Title: How a digital bank's collapse toppled Paraguay's president
Article:
FOR years, Paraguay's digital bank, Ueno, stood out as a homegrown success story, luring roughly half the country's people to open accounts and offering many the opportunity to hold a bank account for the very first time.
But over just five days this week, the bank collapsed, freezing the savings of nearly three million customers — in a country of 6.5 million people — and triggering the country's deepest political crisis in more than a decade.
On Friday evening, President Santiago Pena was impeached after attempting to resign, and his vice president, Pedro Alliana, was sworn in as his replacement.
Authorities quickly arrested Pena, an economist and close ally of US President Donald Trump, and prosecutors charged him on Saturday with breach of trust and administration for personal gain.
A judge ordered him held in pretrial detention at a military facility.
Pena has denied wrongdoing and his attorney, Ricardo Preda, told journalists that he was pleading not guilty to the charges.
The scandal has triggered public protests and sharp rebukes from the opposition.
"We are facing the biggest corruption scandal in our democratic history," said opposition Senator Rafael Filizzola on Friday.
"This impeachment is a first step toward ensuring justice is served."
Manuel Ferreira, a Paraguayan economist and former finance minister, echoed much of the public anger over the case.
"This was a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde," he said.
"They didn't rob us with a pistol, they robbed us with an app. The head of the gang was the president of the republic."
Until March 2025, Pena had been a business partner of the group that owns ueno. After his election in 2023, he tapped Ueno's former president, Carlos Carvallo, to lead the central bank.
Carvallo resigned as central bank chief earlier this week. Prosecutors charged him on Saturday with breach of trust, producing false public documents and administration for personal gain.
[[nid:1573740]]
They sought his pretrial detention, which was approved by a judge.
Carvallo did not respond to a request for comment. It was not immediately clear if he had entered a plea in the case.
Pena's lawyer, Preda, objected to the impeachment, saying that ousting a president during a bank resolution could itself be destabilising.
"What sets a serious country apart is not that its banks don't fail, but how it responds," Preda said on Friday.
"If there is one thing that undermines confidence in the financial system, it is attempting to oust the president without evidence."
Ueno was launched in 2021 as a sleek, millennial-friendly banking app that quickly won over Paraguayans who had been underserved by brick-and-mortar institutions.
It soon became deeply embedded in Paraguay's payments system. It paired its digital offering with physical branches, later sponsoring sports teams, businesses and events.
As of June, public institutions — including Paraguay's state pension fund — held roughly US$850 million in accounts with the bank.
But in recent months, internal regulatory reports warning of excessive lending to certain companies were leaked to local media outlets ABC and Última Hora, triggering political scrutiny of the bank's lending practices.
Following growing public pressure, Paraguay's central bank on Tuesday put ueno into resolution — its strongest measure ‌short of immediate liquidation — after determining that Ueno had breached minimum solvency requirements, locking ​millions of customers temporarily out of their accounts.
The central bank said on Saturday that the equivalent of US$160 million had since been paid out to nearly 1.2 million savers under the state deposit guarantee scheme.
Authorities have promised that depositors will be reimbursed and say the crisis is confined to Ueno. But analysts say the damage to Paraguay's reputation as a stable investment destination in South America may linger far longer than the bank resolution itself.
"This is the moment when Paraguay must demonstrate that its institutions are functioning," Ferreira said.
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mexico arrests another major Jalisco Cartel kingpin
Article:
MEXICO CITY: Mexican authorities announced on Sunday the arrest of a regional leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), one of the country's two main criminal groups.
The CJNG was designated a "foreign terrorist organisation" by the American government in 2025 and is known for its violent tactics and attacks on authorities.
It competes with the Sinaloa Cartel for drug trafficking into the United States, but since the death of its founder, Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera, in a military operation in February, several of its top leaders have been apprehended.
The arrested suspect is Rafael Alvarez, alias "R2," who headed a cell linked to homicides, drug trafficking and extortion of avocado industry entrepreneurs.
The drug gang operates in the states of Jalisco and Michoacan.
Alvarez is also linked to the killing a year ago of Carlos Manzo, a popular mayor known for the way he confronted organized crime.
The kingpin was wounded in a shootout that broke out during the operation to capture him and is receiving medical care, Mexico's Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said on X.
The trafficker was located thanks to information shared by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the official added.
Another 19 people were arrested along with Alvarez, he said.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From scandalous game to mass entertainment: is GTA going soft?
Article:
PARIS: From 24-hour news channel parodies and extreme stereotypes to a twisted Statue of Liberty, the Grand Theft Auto series has consistently mocked the excesses of US capitalist society.
But with days to go before the release of the hugely popular video game's new instalment, players and analysts are wondering if changes in studio Rockstar's creative team suggest a possible shift into less controversial territory, and an end to the punk-rock transgressions that helped turn GTA into a cultural phenomenon.
In marketing and communications leading up to the release of the new "GTA VI" on Nov 19, Rockstar seems keener to steer the conversation toward its Bonnie-and-Clyde-style protagonists trying to survive in a fictionalised, crime-ravaged Miami.
"It's a valid question," said expert Olivier Mauco, author of the book "GTA IV, the Dark Side of the American Dream", noting the various presentations of the new game had so far put the franchise's famed political incorrectness "much less front and centre."
Looking for an explanation for the possible toning-down, Chris Klippel, founder of the specialist outlet Rockstar Mag, noted that "of the five writers who worked on GTA V, three have left," including Dan Houser, one of the two brothers who founded the studio.
"So that inevitably raises concerns."
For expert Christopher Dring, GTA's "punk rock" style is part of Rockstar's DNA.
"That's the whole idea behind them. They know they're middle fingers to the establishment.
"They like making cultural moments. They like people talking about them. They won't play it safe, and if they do, it will be disappointing."
[[nid:1573733]]
- Criticism and controversy -
GTA's taste for transgression goes back to the very first instalment, in 1997.
"To get people talking about them and come across as the bad boys of the industry, the Houser brothers made it seem like GTA was encouraging kids to steal cars," said Mauco.
The bad-boy reputation stuck to the series, which has been regularly accused of glorifying violence and inciting criminal behaviour, even as it became a symbol of rebellious culture.
Starting with "Vice City" (2002) and "San Andreas" (2004), Rockstar gradually began weaving social issues into its gangster stories.
The turning point came with "GTA IV", released in 2008, which features a protagonist — an immigrant from Eastern Europe — trapped in a spiral of violence as he confronts the flip side of the American dream.
"It's certainly the most thoroughly written in terms of social critique," said Mauco.
"It's practically an auteur game, which is pretty wild and paradoxical because even back then it was already one of the most expensive games ever developed."
- Walking a tightrope -
Released in 2013, the next instalment, "GTA V", involves a microcosm of US class warfare with stereotypes on both sides: left-leaning urbane hipsters pitted against Midwestern rednecks.
For Mauco, it portrayed "an America that no longer talks to itself", three years before Donald Trump won the White House.
Although the game has since sold more than 230 million copies, it is difficult to gauge how much gamers cared about its political message.
A lot of GTA's players "are mostly there to blow off steam" and unleash chaos in these vast fictional metropolises, said Klippel.
"I still think it's going to remain very satirical — that's the whole appeal of the series," said Dring, an expert for specialist outlet The Game Business.
Dring compared GTA's biting humour to that of the cartoon "South Park", and warned against expecting direct attacks on Trump or Russia in "GTA VI."
He predicted instead "a critical look at culture and society", starting with the omnipresence of social media.
"GTA has always managed to find the right balance: a world that invites escapism while poking fun at the problems of the modern world."
A thorny tightrope to walk if the game wants to avoid being accused of having a political agenda — a major no-no for many of its biggest fans.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump: Offer of White House press secretary role to Dana White was a joke
Article:
WEST PALM BEACH: US President Donald Trump said Sunday that he was only joking when he offered the role of White House press secretary to Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White earlier in the weekend.
"I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Trump told reporters on the tarmac of his namesake airport in Florida.
The press secretary role – traditionally the most visible administration role after the president – has been vacant since Katie Zacharia stepped down on October 16 after less than a week on the job.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police raid home of ex-president of Paraguay
Article:
ASUNCION: Police in Paraguay raided the home of ex-president Santiago Pena as part of a probe into a banking crisis that triggered his dismissal from office and criminal charges against him.
Authorities last week intervened to seize Ueno Bank, a popular online lender that held accounts for nearly half of Paraguay's 6.5 million people, plus more than US$800 million in government funds.
Its collapse rocked this small, normally stable country, leading to street protests. Pena is now being held in custody at a military facility.
Pena, who came to power in 2023, owned shares in the bank's holding company, Ueno Holding, until he sold them last year.
He is accused of using his influence as president to steer millions in government deposits to Ueno Bank and of hiding or downplaying its financial woes even though he was warned about questionable loans and solvency issues.
Prosecutors announced in a statement that Pena's home was raided as part of the probe into the bank collapse.
They say Ueno Bank received deposits from government entities even as it granted questionable loans to companies linked to Ueno executives.
Pena's mansion outside Asuncion is part of the probe. The indictment says that in 2024 he received two loans from Ueno Bank totaling around US$500,000 so he could build the house.
His monthly mortgage payment is US$38,000 – six times his monthly salary as president, the charging sheet says.
The Senate voted Friday to dismiss Pena, and Vice President Pedro Alliana took his place.
Alliana said Sunday the government has reimbursed 1.2 million Ueno Bank customers whose money was frozen in the collapse.
The disbursal totals around US$158 million so far, and it will continue this week, he said. - AFP PIC
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teenage girl dies in fall from ninth floor of parking lot
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A 17-year-old girl was found dead early yesterday at the Selasih 1Malaysia Civil Servants Housing Project (PPA1M) in Presint 17.
She is believed to have fallen from the ninth floor of the PPA1M's parking structure.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said the victim was found unconscious about 5.45am.
He said the teen was pronounced dead at the scene.
"The case has been classified as a sudden death report (SDR) as no foul play is believed to have occurred. However, further investigations are being conducted," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11 cars, 23 motorcycles destroyed in fire at workshop
Article:
ALOR STAR: Eleven cars and 23 motorcycles were destroyed when a workshop in Kampung Jerang Belangga, Kota Sarang Semut, caught fire early today.
The workshop was about 90 per cent razed in the 3.30am incident.
The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department said firemen from the Guar Cempedeka, Pendang and Jalan Raja stations arrived at the scene about 20 minutes after a distress call was received.
It said no casualties were reported in the incident.
"The fire was brought under control at 3.53am. Twenty firement were involved in the operation. They were assisted by 10 volunteer firemen and the police," it said in a statement.
The cause of the fire and the cost of damages are still being ascertained.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 24 families lose everything in fire at Kanowit longhouse
Article:
KANOWIT: Twenty-four families were left with just the clothes on their backs when the longhouse where they lived in Tuai Rumah Seliau, Sungai Tuah, burnt down early today.
A Fire and Rescue Department spokesman said the fire was reported at 1.39am, adding that firemen arrived at the scene at 2.30am.
The firemen, he said, were from the Kanowit and Sibu Jaya stations.
He added that the blaze was brought under control at 3.53am.
The spokesman said no injuries or deaths were reported in the incident.
The operation involved 16 firemen in two Light Fire Rescue Tenders and a pickup truck.
The cause of the fire and cost of damages have yet to be determined.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four boat skippers, 30 undocumented migrants nabbed at illegal jetty in Nibong
Article:
TANAH MERAH: Four men believed to be boat skippers were detained alongside 30 undocumented migrants from Myanmar in an operation at the Yuti illegal jetty in Nibong yesterday.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Haki Hasbullah said the raid kicked off at 9.45am based on police intelligence.
"Checks at the location led police to the arrests of 34 people, including 30 undocumented migrants comprising 18 men and 12 women from Myanmar.
"The others were Malaysian men believed to have brought the migrants over to the country, with three of these men also testing positive for drug use," he said.
Haki said police also found a bottle containing what is believed to be 450ml of ketum juice in a Perodua Myvi parked nearby.
He said police seized both the Myvi and a Honda City found at the scene.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act, Dangerous Drugs Act and Poison Act.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian embassy monitoring situation in Krakow after shooting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian embassy in Warsaw is closely monitoring the situation in Krakow following a shooting incident at the Main Market Square on Saturday.
The embassy said it remained in contact with the Malaysian community in Krakow to ensure their safety.
"Malaysians in Poland are also encouraged to register their details with the embassy," the embassy said in a Facebook post last night.
The embassy also extended its thoughts and deepest condolences to the victims, their families and the people of Poland during this difficult period of national grief.
"Malaysia stands in solidarity with Poland against such senseless acts of violence."
Malaysians requiring emergency consular assistance may contact the embassy at +48 22 617 4413 during office hours or +48 660 627 360 to reach the officer on duty.
They may also contact the embassy via email at mwwarsaw@kln.gov.my.
In the incident on Nov 7 afternoon, a gunman, reportedly inspired by far-right ideology, killed six people, including a Briton, and injured many others in Krakow, Poland's second-largest city.
According to international media reports citing police, the attacker drove into Main Market Square before opening fire at people in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A-G flags flaws in Najib's house arrest documents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Attorney-general Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar yesterday questioned the diligence exercised in preparing official judicial documents for the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest order.
Commenting on  the Kuala Lumpur High Court's Order of Discharge relating to the former prime minister's sentence, which has raised questions among legal practitioners, he said such issues should not have arisen had the parties involved  scrutinised every detail.
Dusuki said the defects identified in the document were glaring and should not have occurred.
"This should not have happened if the parties concerned had been careful. The mistake is glaring and has caused unnecessary problems," he said.
The defects in question relate particularly to the accuracy of the terminology and legal provisions used in the document.
The document was issued by the High Court after the RM50 million fine imposed on the former Pekan member of parliament, as a condition for serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, was paid using funds collected through the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund launched by Umno.
However, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC)  moved to temporarily suspend the implementation of Najib's house arrest to allow the prosecution to seek further clarification on the actual interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
[[nid:1573703]]
The A-GC's decision drew criticism from Istana Negara, which said any arguments disputing the conditional pardon granted to Najib could amount to defying the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's decree.
Istana Negara stressed that all conditions stipulated in the conditional pardon order had been fulfilled and that its implementation should not give rise to prolonged confusion or uncertainty.
It also maintained that the pardon order was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and had no bearing on any other cases involving Najib.
On the audience with Sultan Ibrahim, Dusuki declined to comment further.
However, it is understood that the audience could take place tomorrow.
On Sept 18, Najib, 73, who is a former Umno president, received a conditional pardon from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
He was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million after being found guilty by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on July 28, 2020, on seven charges relating to the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International.
On Aug 23, 2022, the Federal Court dismissed Najib's final appeal and upheld his conviction and sentence. He began serving his prison term at Kajang Prison on the same day.
He subsequently submitted a pardon petition to the king on Sept 2, 2022. The application was considered at a Pardons Board meeting on Jan 29, 2024.
On Feb 2, 2024, the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department announced the Pardons Board's decision to reduce Najib's prison sentence from 12 years to six years, while the fine was reduced from RM210 million to RM50 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Freiburg third after beating Union, Leverkusen beat Cologne in derby
Article:
BERLIN: Freiburg kept hot on the heels of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund with a comfortable 2-0 home win over lowly Union Berlin to return to third in the Bundesliga table on Sunday, while Bayer Leverkusen sunk derby rivals Cologne.
Freiburg pressured Union captain Rani Khedira into an own goal nine minutes after half-time and Yuito Suzuki scored another as the hosts won despite their own skipper Vincenzo Grifo missing a penalty.
Last season's beaten Europa League finalists are third on 19 points, two behind Bayern and Dortmund with the Bavarians ahead on goal difference.
"We knew our chances would come and we managed to convert them well," Freiburg winger Derry Scherhant told DAZN.
After an even first-half, Freiburg were impressive after the break and forced a last-ditch intervention from Khedira, who knocked the ball into his own net.
Scherhant chipped for Suzuki to score with 67 minutes gone. The Black Forest side may have won by a higher margin were it not for Union goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow, who kept out Grifo's 84th-minute penalty and made a number of other saves.
Earlier on Sunday, goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne which lifted the visitors to fifth in the table.
The fiery encounter produced 11 yellow cards, including six for the home side.
One of several derbies in Germany's football-mad north-west, Cologne and Leverkusen are just 10 kilometres (six miles) apart.
The travelling support teased the hosts with chants referring to the 2023-24 season, when Leverkusen won their maiden Bundesliga title and Cologne were relegated.
Leverkusen broke the deadlock just seven minutes in when Garcia's free-kick flew over the wall and into the top-left corner, with a helpless Cologne goalie Marvin Schwaebe watching on.
Just before the break, the Spaniard found Jarell Quansah in space but the England centre-back headed just wide.
Well handled by the Leverkusen defence, the hosts grew increasingly frustrated, picking up five of their six yellow cards in the second-half.
Schick had a goal ruled out for handball with ten minutes to go but broke through just five minutes later, slotting in on the counter for an eighth goal in nine league appearances this season.
Germany winger Said El Mala scored one of his own in stoppage time but the goal came too late to launch a Cologne comeback and left the hosts stranded in 15th, two points above Union who sit in the relegation play-off spot.
In Sunday's late game, Hoffenheim won 2-1 at promoted Schalke, with Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle getting on the scoresheet for the hosts. --AFP

Title: Rubio: Progress made on 'security infrastructure' after Ukraine war
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday that some progress has been made on what the "security infrastructure" of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia, adding that talks this week could lead to further advances.
Rubio's comments, ahead of his travel to Paris for talks with G7 foreign ministers, come as Russia-Ukraine negotiations under US mediation have been set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi.
The need for security guarantees is an issue that has come up repeatedly in talks about ending the conflict, Rubio told reporters, referring to the war that broke out after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
A key issue is, he said, "What is the postwar security infrastructure of Ukraine and more broadly of the European continent going to look like?"
"I think that's what the president's alluding to – is that there's been some advances made in what that architecture could look like post-conflict," he added.
US President Donald Trump on Thursday predicted a "very big" deal with Moscow involving not only Ukraine but "all of Europe," in remarks likely to fuel fresh fears of a pivot towards the Kremlin.
Rubio said on Sunday that "nothing's been finalised yet, and maybe some progress can be made in Abu Dhabi."
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump's son-in-law, are expected to represent the United States in Abu Dhabi.--AFP

Title: Timeless principles of true leadership
Article:
LETTERS:
Selangor recently marked a truly historic milestone as the state celebrated the Silver Jubilee of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah.
The celebration commemorates 25 years of steady and wise leadership. Reflecting on this quarter-century, many people highlighted the Sultan's deep love for everyone he serves.
In a special anniversary interview, the ruler shared thoughts that deeply touched the public. He reminded everyone that Selangor's greatest strength is not just its business and economic success.
Instead, its true strength is its diverse people—from every race, faith, and background—living, working, and building a better future together.
The Sultan also delivered a clear and important message against mixing race and religion into politics.
This message struck a chord with citizens who are tired of division and arguments. He stood up for harmony, respect, and decency, reminding everyone that differences are what make the community strong and should never be used to tear people apart.
In addition, the ruler spoke about good governance. He expressed concern over the proper management of financial funds like Tabung Haji.
He reminded the public that money given for religious purposes must be handled with total honesty, great care, and full accountability so that public trust is never broken.
The Sultan also emphasised that real progress means nothing if it does not help everyone. His ongoing care for the poor, the vulnerable, and those who might be left behind brings deep reassurance. It proves that no one is forgotten under his watch.
Finally, he gave timeless advice on what good leadership means: to listen carefully before making decisions, to stay humble no matter how much success comes, to follow the Constitution, and always to put the interests of the people first.
As Selangor looks ahead, people thanked the Sultan for his caring heart and his steady hand. They offered prayers for his continued good health, great wisdom, and strength as he leads the state forward.
Daulat Tuanku!
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Kuala Lumpur

Title: CAAM targets year-end framework to scale up Malaysia's low-altitude economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is preparing an initial framework for its low-altitude economy (LAE) by year-end as it moves towards limited commercial operations in the first quarter of 2027.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the framework is aims to provide a common direction for government agencies, industry players, manufacturers and operators as Malaysia scales up the use of low-altitude airspace while maintaining safety and public confidence.
"The initial framework we are targeting by end of this year…Initial framework means we need to get all the stakeholders at least to be aware," he told Business Times in an interview recently.
LAE refers to economic and public service activities conducted within low-altitude airspace using emerging aviation technologies and services.
These include drones or unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), advanced air mobility (AAM), urban air mobility, autonomous serial logistics, future air taxi services, infrastructure inspection and emergency response operations.
Norazman said normal civil aviation traffic generally operates above 4000 feet except around airport areas, leaving lower-altitude airspace that could be used for other applications.
"Most of this area at 1000 metres and below or 3000-4000 feet are not used. A lot of applications that you can use below this altitude outside of the airport area."
"For example, we can do surveillance; we can do cargo; lots of drones or flying machines that can be used to do this and also advanced air mobility like air taxi can use this range of altitude," he said.
Malaysia launched its national LAE initiative on June 24 at the inaugural LAE Forum 2026, organised by CAAM and launched by Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
The Transport Ministry has entrusted CAAM with spearheading the development of the regulatory, operational and governance framework required to support the country's LAE ecosystem.
Norazman said about 14 ministries are involved in LAE and a common framework is needed to coordinate the various stakeholders as the industry develops.
He said the ecosystem also involves government agencies, technology providers, aircraft manufacturers, operators and users, requiring the various parties to move in the same direction.
"If everybody is heading in different directions, how do you actually want to scale up this industry? So, everybody needs to move in the correct direction. How are people going to move in the correct direction?"
"You have to do a blueprint. You have to do a framework on how you actually can expand this," he said.
Four Phase Of LAE Roadmap
CAAM's strategic roadmap set out four phases for developing the sector.
The first began with LAE Forum 2026 as a platform to introduce the initiative and engage government agencies, industry, academia, technology providers and investors.
The next phase involves setting up a multi-stakeholder task force to coordinate policy development, regulatory planning and stakeholder collaboration.
This is followed by a national operational demonstration of low-altitude aviation technologies and a second LAE Forum before limited commercial operations are introduced under a controlled and regulated environment in the first quarter of 2027.
From small-scale low-altitude aviation operations to wider use across various industries
Norazman said Malaysia already has several low-altitude aviation activities operating on a smaller scale, including drone surveillance, agriculture, cargo and entertainment.
"We already have, but all on a smaller scale and different places. We already have surveillance approved. Petronas is doing gas pipeline surveillance. Agriculture, we already have a lot of agriculture activities, especially in the north."
"We are venturing into cargo, sending small cargo of 50-100 kilogrammes. In terms of entertainment, there are swarm drones," he said.
One of the applications being explored is the use of drones to transport medicines and medical samples, particularly from rural and remote areas where land transportation takes longer.
Norazman said a proof of concept involving hospitals is being carried out in Sabah to transport samples from remote communities.
"At this moment, what we are looking at, which is more critical, is delivering medicines, delivering samples," he said.
Norazman also said drones capable of carrying between 50kg and 500kg are available, although smaller payloads could provide a starting point for such operations.
"We can do 50, 100kg within a 100-kilometre radius. That's very, very feasible rather than if you use road, it probably takes one day (to deliver)," he said.
While these activities are already taking place on a smaller scale, Norazman said the next challenge is to expand them and integrate low-altitude operations within Malaysia's existing civil aviation ecosystem.
"But how do you actually scale this up, make it in a safe environment? How can the activities of this low-altitude economy blend in with the existing civil aviation ecosystem?" he added.
Scaling Up LAE Ecosystem
Beyond aircraft and pilots, Norazman said scaling up LAE requires telecommunications and data infrastructure, maintenance personnel, operational planning and continuous training.
"For drone operation, telecommunications are very important, data centres are very important. But as you scale up, you need support beyond the pilot as well. Currently, there are more than 6000 rated drone pilots. But you have to think of who is going to maintain (the drones)?" he said.
He said training and skills development also have to extend beyond drone pilots.
"The training is continuous. You have to keep building the capacity not just in flying (but) in maintenance, all sorts of things. These are the kind of ecosystem, the support that needs to be built," he said.
The wider LAE ecosystem identified by CAAM includes UAS traffic management, communications and connectivity, navigation and surveillance, take-off and landing infrastructure, data and cloud services, skills development, investment, research and development and legal and regulatory frameworks.
Norazman said CAAM's regulatory approach has to balance the development of new technology with safety requirements without imposing controls that could unnecessarily restrict growth.
"As a safety and security regulator, that is our main aim. We are not against making the technology grow. We cannot be over-regulating as well, that distorts the growth."
"But you need people to be aware there are some sort of controls, that it is not free-for-all," he said.
Path For Businesses
For small and medium enterprises and start-ups seeking to conduct drone operations in sectors such as logistics and agriculture, Norazman said operators first need a clear concept of operations (CONOPS).
He said this sets out what an operator plans to do, including the type of cargo it plans to carry, its weight, operating range and the type of aircraft required.
"For any type of operation, you need a concept of operations. How are you going to operate?"
"Let's say you are interested in the delivery business. What kind of cargo do you want to carry? What type of weight do you want to carry? What type of range do you want to cover?" he said.
He said certification requirements depend on the aircraft and the type of operation with higher risks associated with heavier and more complex aircraft.
CAAM has also expanded its drone unit as the sector develops.
Norazman said the unit had grown from one officer when he joined CAAM in 2022 to more than 10 people with personnel receiving continuous training in areas including certification and Specific Operations Risk Assessment (SORA).
CAAM said LAE has the potential to create new economic opportunities and skilled jobs, improve productivity and operational efficiency, support technology adoption and improve public services and connectivity.
Air Taxis After 2028
On passenger-carrying air taxis, Norazman said such services are likely to come later as manufacturers are still working towards certification of their aircraft.
"I would say after 2028. Why? Because in terms of certification, I don't think anyone has one that is certified to fly people yet. Most of the advanced original equipment manufacturers are in the stages of certifying their machines," he said.

Title: Wage hike may push plantation costs up 9pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's plantation sector faces mounting cost pressures from higher minimum wages, with the likes of SD Guthrie Bhd estimating a potential nine per cent increase in its overall costs.
Under the 2027 Budget, the government proposed raising the minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000.
Industry players said the increase is expected to raise labour costs for plantation companies, which have limited ability to pass on higher expenses as crude palm oil (CPO) prices are largely determined by global market conditions.
Malaysian Palm Oil Association (MPOA) chief executive Roslin Azmy Hassan said plantation companies will have to absorb most of the additional expenses, putting pressure on profit margins, particularly if CPO prices remain subdued.
He said the impact will vary depending on companies' workforce structures, productivity, operational efficiency and prevailing CPO prices, with smaller operators likely to face greater challenges due to tighter margins.
"Larger plantation companies may be better placed to absorb these additional costs, while smaller operators with tighter margins will find it more challenging," he told Business Times.
SD Guthrie estimated that the higher minimum wage could increase its overall costs by about nine per cent, based on a preliminary assessment assuming the impact takes effect in the second half of 2027.
The fully integrated palm oil producer said about 36,600 of its workers in Malaysia are expected to be affected by the increase.
The company said it supports fair and progressive wage growth as part of building a productive and sustainable workforce, consistent with its Living Wage Policy, which is being implemented in phases.
The policy will initially cover about 8,000 non-plantation employees in Malaysia, with implementation targeted for completion by December 2026.
SD Guthrie said higher labour costs would accelerate efforts to improve productivity through mechanisation, better tools, enhanced skills and more efficient estate operations.
"The long-term solution lies in increasing productivity, enabling workers to generate greater value while earning better incomes," it said.
LIMITED ROOM TO PASS ON COSTS
Roslin said it was difficult to identify a specific CPO price that will fully offset higher labour expenses because production costs, yields and labour requirements differ significantly between companies.
Plantation companies are price takers, leaving them with little control over the prices they receive for their output, he added.
He said stronger and more stable CPO prices will help cushion the impact, but companies also need sufficient margins to finance replanting, mechanisation and productivity improvements while meeting their responsibilities towards workers.
Meanwhile, SD Guthrie considers a CPO price range of RM2,500 to RM4,500 per tonne sustainable.
It said prices below RM2,500 per tonne could place producers under significant pressure relative to their cost base.
Prices above RM5,000 per tonne might prove unsustainable as palm oil becomes less competitive against alternative vegetable oils, potentially weakening demand.
The company said it was too early to determine the CPO price needed to offset the higher wage bill, with its strategy instead focused on improving productivity, mechanisation and operational efficiency.
"Expanding our portfolio of differentiated and specialised products remains an important strategy to help protect margins across commodity cycles.
"Our approach is centred on building a more resilient and productive business that can perform well across varying commodity price environments," it said.
MECHANISATION KEY TO PRODUCTIVITY
Roslin said plantation companies would need to prioritise productivity and operational efficiency rather than rely solely on cost-cutting measures to protect earnings in 2028.
These efforts include improving harvesting efficiency, reducing crop losses, making better use of available workers and raising fresh fruit bunch (FFB) yields through improved estate management and agronomic practices.
He said mechanisation remained part of the solution, although harvesting continued to depend largely on manual labour and reliable, commercially viable harvesting machines were still being developed.
"Through initiatives such as Mechanisation and Automation Research Consortium of Oil Palm, MPOA is working with industry players to develop practical mechanisation solutions that can help reduce our dependence on manual labour over time," he said.
Roslin also warned that insufficient harvesters could lead to harvesting delays and crop losses, further undermining productivity and earnings.
SD Guthrie said its measures would include mechanising estate upkeep activities such as pesticide application, manuring, pruning and estate clearing, as well as improving the area each worker could manage effectively.
It will also focus on maintaining accessible and well-managed estates to improve harvesting efficiency, alongside disciplined replanting and the use of higher-yielding planting materials.
Both MPOA and SD Guthrie said it was too early to quantify the savings expected from these initiatives, given differences in estate conditions, productivity levels and the pace of technology adoption.
Roslin said the government's intention to improve workers' wages and welfare needed to be accompanied by productivity gains, particularly as the plantation sector faced labour shortages, rising compliance costs and increasingly stringent sustainability requirements.
"At the end of the day, we need to strike a balance between better wages for workers and keeping our plantation industry competitive and sustainable in the long run," he said.
He added that future wage adjustments should take into account the industry's operating realities, particularly plantation companies' limited control over CPO prices.

Title: PNB unfazed by MSCI's Indonesia concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) has ruled out a blanket withdrawal from Indonesian investments following MSCI's proposal to reclassify the country's equity market, saying the index provider's concerns do not, by themselves, justify an exit.
PNB said it has no direct holdings in Indonesian equities. Its direct exposure to the country is limited to fixed-income investments that account for a very small proportion of its total assets under management.
MSCI's latest move, announced on Oct 15, proposes reclassifying Indonesia from an emerging market to a standalone market, citing persistent concerns over opaque shareholding structures, suspected coordinated trading and weaknesses in market governance.
This triggered a sharp sell-off in the market. Indonesia's benchmark Jakarta Composite Index saw the largest single-day drop on Oct 16 since January 1998 after about US$65 billion was wiped off the value of Indonesian stocks.
MSCI also said market participants had yet to see sufficient evidence that reforms announced by Indonesian authorities had materially improved market transparency and functioning.
The proposal marks an escalation of concerns first raised in January, when MSCI froze certain index-related changes involving Indonesian securities while awaiting improvements in free-float data and shareholder disclosures.
Indonesia has since introduced measures including disclosure of shareholders with stakes above one per cent, a framework to monitor high shareholding concentration and a roadmap to raise minimum free float to 15 per cent.
MSCI is consulting market participants until April 30, 2027, and is expected to announce its final decision by June 30. It has also maintained the freeze on certain index changes in the meantime.
PNB said the downgrade by the global index provider is one of the many factors the fund looks at before investing with other reasons also coming into play.
"The proposed reclassification by MSCI is one of many factors PNB considers alongside economic fundamentals, valuation, liquidity, governance standards, regulatory developments, and long-term prospects of the country," PNB said in a response to Business Times' queries.
PNB said uncertainties over market accessibility, governance, foreign investor participation, currency stability and policy direction would need to be weighed against company-specific fundamentals.
On its investment in Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), which has exposure to Indonesia through PT Maybank Indonesia Tbk, PNB said it remained confident in the group's management and board to strengthen operational performance, manage risks and enhance shareholder value.
PNB described its Maybank investment as a long-term strategic holding and said it would engage constructively with the group through established governance channels, while respecting the board and management's authority over its subsidiaries.

Title: Nvidia probes CEO Huang amid reports of Chinese spy links to Singapore-based firm
Article:
NEW YORK: Chip giant Nvidia's board announced Sunday it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence.
Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that the woman, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing.
The executive, Alice Huang – also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang – developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.
In a message to company employees released Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologised to both his family and company staff.
"I was unfaithful to my wife," he said. "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
Asked about the report Sunday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he couldn't comment, saying it was an "internal corporate matter."
Jensen Huang is a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and close to President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race.
The Times said Huang's relationship with the other Huang could have given her insights into Trump's thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump's planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China.
Nvidia said in a statement it opened an independent probe "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." It did not name a country.
The statement added: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."
The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as "groundless speculation."
- 'BLACK EYE MOMENT' -
China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.
Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world's most valuable companies.
Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter.
Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang's relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said.
Technology analyst Dan Ives, with the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said word of the probe is "a black eye moment" for Jensen Huang.
Ives predicted it will at the very least spark multiple congressional inquiries and "create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons."
In the near-term Huang is expected to keep his job but risks being removed as Nvidia's CEO depending on the board's probe, Ives said in a statement.
"This will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally," he said. "This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China, which remains a key battleground issue in DC."--AFP

Title: Pope takes Milei to task over cuts affecting Argentina's poor
Article:
BUENOS AIRES: Pope Leo XIV delivered a stinging critique of President Javier Milei's harsh austerity measures Sunday, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause.
"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," he said, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.
Leo stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."
He spoke out in defence of the poor and pensioners, insisting that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" – a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.
And he told Milei, known for his foul-mouthed diatribes, that strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words."
The visit is the first by a pontiff to Argentina in nearly four decades and Leo was met with calls to help mend deep divisions in the country after three years of austerity under Milei.
Leo arrived in Buenos Aires from Uruguay where he began his first trip to Latin America as pope, the world's most Catholic continent that is becoming increasingly secular.
The visit is the first by a pontiff to the home country of the late pope Francis in nearly four decades.
Milei famously insulted Francis for his pro-poor teachings. Leo said he was "retracing" Francis's steps.
- 'UNITE US' -
Argentines are hoping the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics will help unite the country, which is bitterly divided between supporters and opponents of Milei.
"Just like the World Cup unites us, hopefully the pope will too," said Liliana Deblauwe, a 68-year-old retired teacher who waited with hundreds of people to see the pope visit a monument to liberation hero Jose de San Martin.
Hundreds more chanting "Papa Leon" (Spanish for Leo) gathered outside the presidential palace, where he was hosted by Milei.
Brian Inacio Rodriguez, a 26-year-old job seeker, spent five days travelling overland from Ushuaia, at the very tip of South America, to see the pontiff.
He said he hoped he brought "much peace to Argentina."
Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, Pope Leo is on an ambitious 12-day tour of the continent where he served nearly two decades as a missionary.
In Uruguay, he condemned drug violence and urged an end to child poverty.
The Argentine stage of his visit aims to boost the flagging faith of a country left disappointed by Francis's failure to visit during his papacy.
It will also act as a litmus test of support for the Church.
Some 57.7 percent of people identified as Catholic in a recent University of Buenos Aires poll, down from around 90 per cent in the 1960s.
Leo will visit a home for disabled people and a prison and celebrate three open-air masses.
The Church has said it expects a total of seven million faithful at the various events.
- 'IMBECILE' FRANCIS -
Milei came to office on a promise to revive Argentina's ailing economy and tame runaway inflation by shrinking the welfare state, targeting public hospitals, universities and pensioners in particular.
The poverty rate has swung wildly since he came to power – increasing to 32.3 per cent in September.
A close ally of US President Donald Trump, with a similar combative style, Milei had a tense relationship with Francis.
On the campaign trail the cost-cutting economist called his countryman an "imbecile" for championing social justice.
Once in office, however, he softened his tone but he continues to heap insults on the press and opposition.
His relationship with Leo has so far been cordial, but the local Catholic Church has heavily criticised him for treating key social services solely as a budgetary constraint.
Milei has also been criticised for restricting several democratic freedoms, including the right to protest. But he maintains a loyal supporter base for drastically reducing inflation.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Make Sarawak's wealth work harder
Article:
A MAJOR investment should be judged partly by what it builds in the surrounding economy after construction is complete.
For Sarawak, the lasting return should include competitive local suppliers and people whose skills command higher wages.
That is a practical test of resource-led development. An industrial facility may produce for decades. Its contribution becomes broader when local firms acquire the ability to service it, workers progress into skilled positions and those capabilities find customers beyond the original project.
Sarawak's Post Covid-19 Development Strategy 2030 already connects economic prosperity with social inclusivity and environmental sustainability.
Delivering that ambition requires clear measures of what major investments contribute to local enterprise, resident earnings and public welfare.
Contracts That Build Capability
The starting point should be the commercial opportunities around established industries.
Oil and gas facilities, power systems and manufacturing plants create demand for maintenance, engineering and specialised services.
Local enterprises can develop around these requirements if they understand the standards expected and can invest with reasonable confidence.
Large companies and public agencies could publish procurement opportunities earlier, explain qualification requirements and offer credible routes for capable smaller firms to compete.
Supplier development should address practical barriers such as certification costs, working capital and access to testing facilities.
Contract terms matter too. A technically competent small company may struggle if payment is slow or a contract requires financing beyond its means.
Prompt payment and appropriately structured contracts can make participation commercially viable without compromising safety or quality.
Local-content targets should be assessed against the value actually created.
A locally registered intermediary selling imported equipment adds a different level of capability from a firm undertaking design, fabrication or technical work. Counting invoices alone can reward the appearance of participation.
Support should therefore have measurable milestones and periodic review. The aim is for firms to improve productivity, secure repeat business and eventually win customers elsewhere.
Continued dependence on protected contracts would indicate that the development effort needs adjustment.
International partnerships can assist this process through shared engineering work, supplier mentoring and commercial technology agreements.
The local contribution should deepen as competence develops. Such arrangements require capable partners and incentives that make learning worthwhile for both sides.
Skills That Raise Earnings
Supplier development will have limited reach if workers cannot acquire the skills these industries require.
Employers, training institutions and universities should jointly identify occupations with sustained demand and design training around the work actually performed.
Apprenticeships and workplace training provide a direct connection between learning and employment.
Programmes should be assessed through completion rates, placement in relevant jobs and subsequent earnings. Enrolment figures alone reveal little about whether training improves a person's prospects.
Participation also depends on circumstances outside the classroom. A rural student may need transport and accommodation. An adult worker may need a flexible timetable or income support during training.
Addressing these barriers would widen access to industrial opportunities beyond those already best placed to obtain them.
The employment objective should include progression. A worker who enters through a basic maintenance role should have a credible route towards technical qualifications and greater responsibility.
Employers should be encouraged to connect recognised skills with better pay as productivity improves.
Resource revenues also provide an opportunity to strengthen the foundations on which enterprise depends. Reliable utilities, education and healthcare support household welfare and productive participation.
The quality of these services matters particularly in communities too distant to benefit directly from an industrial cluster.
Public investment choices should account for operating costs and environmental consequences over the life of a project.
A facility that requires continuing subsidy or imposes substantial costs on surrounding communities may yield a weaker social return than its headline investment value suggests.
Make Federalism Deliver
Sarawak's place in the federation should support this effort. Federal and state institutions bring different responsibilities, resources and expertise.
Cooperation on infrastructure, skills and industrial development can create opportunities that neither level of government could deliver as effectively alone.
Revenue-sharing arrangements and constitutional responsibilities remain important. Their economic value is strengthened when public funds help households and firms acquire lasting earning capacity.
Equally, stronger production links with other states can help Sarawak suppliers reach larger markets.
Better evidence would help organise this cooperation. Malaysia already has national input-output tables and social accounting matrices published by the Statistics Department.
Research by Pang Chun Sian and Mohd Khairul Hisyam Hassan also applies a 2015 interregional framework covering Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.
These are foundations on which to build.
The next step should be a regularly updated official framework connecting production flows between individual states with evidence on household incomes.
A regional social accounting matrix could help examine how wages, business income and transfers reach different household groups.
Modelled benefits should be reported with their assumptions and checked against observed outcomes.
The Statistics Department and Sarawak's economic planners could begin with a joint pilot around a major industrial cluster.
Participating firms could supply consistent procurement and employment data. An annual assessment could then track local value added, resident earnings and suppliers graduating into more demanding contracts.
Such an exercise would give policymakers a practical basis for improving existing programmes. It would show where support produces capability, where barriers remain and which measures deserve expansion.
The decisive test should be whether a young Sarawakian can acquire a useful skill, find productive work and build a secure life at home. That is how the state's wealth can work harder for its people.

Title: Mentakab's last newsdealer keeps print tradition alive [WATCH]
Article:
TEMERLOH: As younger generations embrace digital platforms, 70-year-old K. Mutusamy is determined to keep the tradition of  printed newspapers and magazines alive in Mentakab.
He is the town's only remaining newsdealer, serving a loyal group of customers who still prefer holding a newspaper or magazine in their hands to reading the news on a screen.
Despite the steady decline in demand over the years, Mutusamy has no intention of calling it a day, and is determined to keep his small business running for as long as his health allows.
The father of three, who started selling newspapers and magazines in 1979 before opening his shop in Jalan Tun Abdul Razak in 1987, said the business was more than just a source of income, describing it as a passion he was not ready to give up.
"I have seen the transformation of the newspaper and magazine industry over nearly five decades. There was a time when readers would wait outside my shop as early as 5.30am to buy newspapers, while some even made advance bookings for magazines.
"I remember arriving at the shop around 3am to wait for lorries delivering newspapers from the printing factory before opening for business at 5.30am. Dozens of newspaper agents and paperboys would gather outside the shop to sort out their copies," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Mutusamy said he used to sell more than 70 titles of Malay, English and Tamil magazines, including popular local comics, many of which had since ceased print publication or moved to digital platforms.
"For central Pahang, magazines would first arrive at my shop before other agents came to collect their copies. I remember selling one of the first local English-language women's lifestyle magazines, which was  in high demand.
"Those days, people could be seen standing along the shop corridor, browsing through piles of newspapers in different languages. I used to be busy.
"I sometimes wonder where the years went... time passed so quickly. These days, mostly loyal customers continue to visit the shop," he said, adding that his wife, C. Thanalatchimy, 64, used to help him but now takes care of their grandchildren.
The Perak-born newsdealer said he had focused solely on selling newspapers and magazines because of the overwhelming demand for printed reading materials during the 1980s and 1990s.
"Back then, newspaper agents were common, but over the years, many retired and some ventured into other businesses. I am the only one who is still operating.
"I never explored other business opportunities or considered running a grocery store. I was never prepared for this decline in demand, but people's reading habits have changed."
His eldest son, a medical officer, and  two other children, who work as teachers, continue to help out at the shop.
"A newsdealer cannot afford to close for even a day, or we risk losing customers. I started my life with newspapers, and I intend to continue selling them until my last breath," he said.

Title: Analysts weigh BN-PN and PH manifestos ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA:  The Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional joint election manifesto offers a  structured development agenda for the state,  although Pakatan Harapan has put forward several distinctive proposals aimed at youth entrepreneurship and inclusive economic growth, a political analyst said.
Universiti Malaya senior political science lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the BN-PN manifesto stood out for its measurable economic commitments, particularly its targets
of attracting RM30 billion in investments, creating 25,000 jobs and delivering 25,000 affordable homes over five years.
He said the pledges directly address economic opportunities and living standards, providing clear benchmarks against which the coalition's performance could be assessed.
Tawfik said the proposals on   free water for eligible households and financial assistance for B40 students pursuing technical and vocational education and training courses  were promising.
He said the initiatives could help ease the cost of living while improving employment prospects for the  low-income group.
However, he added, PH's manifesto should not be overlooked, particularly its proposal to allocate 30 per cent of local authority contracts to young people.
He described the initiative as an interesting approach to encouraging youth entrepreneurship and increasing their participation in the local economy.
"PH's proposal to allocate 30 per cent of local authority contracts to young people stands out as an interesting initiative to encourage youth entrepreneurship.
"Its commitment to providing special grants for women entrepreneurs, expanding childcare facilities for working mothers and attracting 25 million tourists by 2032 could also strengthen economic participation."
Tawfik said all coalitions must ensure their commitments translate into tangible improvements in people's lives rather than merely achieving impressive numerical targets.
On criticism that PH repackaged  initiatives introduced by the past   government, Tawfik said there was some merit to the argument.
He said some proposals in PH's manifesto reflected priorities pursued by  previous state administrations.
"For example, PH's Smart Melaka initiative overlaps with the Smart Melaka Blueprint 2035 launched in 2022, while tourism development, affordable housing and public service digitalisation have long been part of the state's development agenda."
Nevertheless, Tawfik said, it would be unfair to dismiss PH's entire manifesto.
Ilham Centre research fellow and political analyst Mujibu Abd Muis said BN was capable of fulfilling its 20 main commitments, based on its financial capacity, realistic planning and effective implementation mechanisms.
"In my view, the manifesto is relatively strong in terms of benefit distribution and welfare.
"People do not just want the cost of living to be reduced through assistance. They also want higher income, quality jobs and wider economic opportunities."
International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said voters who believe BN had been delivering assistance would likely find the joint manifesto sufficient, as their priority was having a government that could continue providing support.
"Why fix what is not broken? At this point, I feel voters have trust in BN-PN as the state government, with BN leading the administration.
"They don't need fancy promises. They just need a government that can provide assistance."
