Title: Melaka election 2026: What the parties are promising, where the battles are and what could decide the vote
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — As campaigning for the 16th Melaka state election enters its second week, rival parties are seeking to win over voters with promises of economic growth, political stability and reform, while new alliances face the test of whether their supporters will vote across party lines.
Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) are banking on their joint electoral machinery, Pakatan Harapan (PH) is challenging the incumbent administration’s record, and smaller parties are seeking to distinguish themselves through reform pledges and alternative campaign strategies.
A total of 79 candidates are contesting 28 state seats in the November 14 election, with early voting scheduled for November 10.
PH is contesting 24 seats, followed by BN with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) with 16, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with seven, PN with five and Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (Putra) with one. Three candidates are running as independents.
Here is how the main parties are making their case, the issues shaping the campaign and the key contests to watch as polling day approaches.
BN-PN: Promising continuity and growth
BN and PN are presenting a united front through their Muafakat Melaka arrangement, with caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh leading their campaign pitch on development and economic growth.
Their joint manifesto promises to attract RM30 billion in investments, provide free domestic water for households consuming less than 20 cubic metres a month and freeze quit rent increases for five years.
Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional are campaigning under the Muafakat Melaka arrangement, promising economic growth and development while seeking to consolidate support among their respective voters. — Bernama pic
Other proposals include establishing Melaka as a national technical and vocational education and training (TVET) hub, providing financial assistance to B40 students pursuing TVET qualifications and offering funding to small traders.
Ab Rauf has also defended his administration’s record, claiming BN has fulfilled 97 per cent of the promises made in its 2021 state election manifesto.
However, PH chairman Adly Zahari has challenged that figure, arguing that BN should account for its earlier commitments before making fresh ones.
BN’s campaign is also seeking to demonstrate unity between Umno and PAS, with their cooperation presented as a continuation of their electoral partnership in Negeri Sembilan.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has urged both parties’ campaign machinery to respect one another and avoid clashes, underscoring the challenge of managing their previous political differences.
Beyond policy announcements, BN has brought familiar faces into its campaign.
After previously enlisting Chinese actress Fan Bingbing to promote Melaka internationally, Ab Rauf brought veteran Malaysian actor Datuk Jalaluddin Hasan to campaign in the Bukit Katil constituency.
At the constituency level, Duyong incumbent Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, who has built a following on social media, said he was not offering a specific manifesto this time, arguing that addressing residents’ problems was already his responsibility as their elected representative.
Pakatan Harapan is seeking to challenge BN’s record in Melaka, focusing on governance, economic opportunities and unfulfilled promises while navigating its partnership with the coalition at the federal level. — Bernama pic
PH: Challenging BN’s record
For PH, the challenge is to convince voters that it offers a credible alternative to BN, despite both coalitions being part of the federal unity government.
Its manifesto,
Aspirasi Melaka Rumah Kita
, is built around three main pillars and 12 priorities, including transparent administration, the Smart Melaka transformation, economic opportunities for young people and stronger tourism development.
The coalition is also targeting younger voters with a proposal to allocate 30 per cent of local authority work contracts to young people, alongside pledges on employment, housing and public welfare.
Prime Minister and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has highlighted the coalition’s multiracial appeal and the integrity of its candidates as key strengths.
PH is making BN’s record in state government a central campaign issue, with Adly repeatedly questioning its delivery of previous manifesto commitments and the lower jobs target in its latest pledges.
The coalition has also been holding daily 10am press conferences at its main operations room in Bukit Baru, featuring Adly, acting Melaka PKR state leadership council chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim and Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong.
The regular briefings allow PH to respond to campaign developments, challenge BN-PN and keep its policy positions in the public eye.
Some PH leaders have also urged voters to assess the coalition based on the federal government’s record, with Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Karim arguing that its national performance should be part of voters’ considerations.
However, PH must distinguish its state-level agenda from BN’s while remaining its partner in Putrajaya, a balancing act that complicates its campaign against the incumbent administration.
Bersatu is contesting seven seats under its own banner, positioning itself as an alternative to BN amid political differences with PAS and the wider Perikatan Nasional alliance. — Picture via Facebook/ts.muhyiddin
Bersatu: Taking on BN amid PAS tensions
Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia is seeking to position itself as an alternative to BN while navigating tensions with PAS that have complicated the PN campaign.
The party is contesting seven seats under its own logo, separately from PN’s five candidates.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said some voters remained confused about the distinction between Bersatu and PN, prompting him to instruct party leaders to clarify its position during the campaign.
At a mega ceramah in Pantai Kundor, Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali accused PAS and Wawasan of betraying the mandate previously given to PN voters by cooperating with parties they had once campaigned against.
He also pointed to political turmoil in Negeri Sembilan, arguing that BN and Umno had failed to provide stable government despite their electoral success there.
Azmin urged Melaka voters not to give BN another opportunity to govern, warning that the state could face similar instability.
Muhyiddin, meanwhile, has returned to a familiar campaign argument by highlighting his record as prime minister during the Covid-19 pandemic, recalling his administration’s handling of the country during the lockdowns.
The approach echoes his previous state election and by-election campaigns since the 15th general election, when his pandemic-era leadership featured prominently in his appeal to voters.
Parti Bersama Malaysia has combined grassroots campaigning with livestreamed ceramah and reform pledges, seeking to reach voters beyond traditional campaign events. — Picture via Facebook/rafiziramli.bersama
Bersama: Reform pledges and digital campaigning
Among the smaller parties, Bersama is combining conventional ceramah and grassroots engagement with an extensive online presence, adopting an approach similar to its previous Johor election campaigns.
The party was the first to launch its manifesto for the Melaka election and has placed reform at the centre of its campaign.
Its
Jelajah Trak Kancil
campaign involves candidates and party leaders holding ceramah from a small truck, usually beginning around 9pm, with the events streamed live on YouTube.
Based on observations of the livestreams, the broadcasts have drawn about 80,000 views each, extending the party’s reach beyond those attending in person.
Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli and his media team have also been accompanying candidates on the ground.
Bersama has revived familiar reform messages from previous elections, including inviting Teoh Lee Lan, the sister of the late Teoh Beng Hock, to one of its campaign events.
All 16 Bersama candidates signed a pledge calling for a fresh investigation into Teoh’s death, the introduction of an Anti-Torture Act and comprehensive reforms of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission.
The party is also using government data to scrutinise the incumbent administration, with Rafizi highlighting what he described as an increasingly unsustainable state financial position.
Bersama has used the figures to call for better revenue collection and a review of spending priorities, reflecting Rafizi’s data-driven approach to scrutinising public administration.
Jobs, the cost of living and the impact of development projects on local communities are among the key concerns shaping voter sentiment ahead of the November 14 polls, according to a political analyst. — Bernama pic
Voter sentiment: Jobs, living costs and stability
Despite the competing political narratives, campaigning has been relatively subdued, with local economic concerns taking precedence over national political rhetoric, according to political analyst Amir Fareed Rahim.
The strategic director of consultancy KRA Group said jobs and the cost of living remained key concerns, but voters were also questioning whether development projects were delivering tangible benefits to local communities.
“From our observation, key issues raised by these voters centre around whether tourism is improving local livelihoods, what coastal reclamation means for fishing communities, and how the state will deal with worsening traffic,” he told
Malay Mail
.
Political stability is another consideration, given that Melaka has had several chief ministers since 2018.
Amir Fareed said criticism of delayed projects could work both ways for BN, raising questions about its delivery while also reminding voters of the importance of continuity.
He said BN had an advantage among voters who credited Ab Rauf with development and welfare initiatives, while PH retained support in areas where its candidates had addressed local grievances.
Non-Malay voters, however, faced a more complicated choice, with some disappointed by the pace of federal reforms while remaining uneasy about Umno’s cooperation with PAS.
That unease could help PH retain support, although disappointment with the federal government’s reform agenda could also affect turnout, he said.
Amir Fareed said BN-PN had the clearest path to forming the state government, citing BN’s incumbency, Ab Rauf’s development record and more coordinated cooperation between Umno and PAS than in the previous two state elections.
The real test, however, would be whether that cooperation translated into votes in constituencies where the parties were supporting one another’s candidates.
Pakatan Harapan candidate for Paya Rumput, Datuk Azman Abidin, watches former national footballers, including Safee Sali and Mat Yo, in action during a football clinic held as part of his Melaka election campaign. Paya Rumput is among the key battlegrounds where voter turnout and shifting political loyalties could influence the outcome of the November 14 polls. — Bernama pic
Key battlegrounds: Where votes could swing
Among the seats to watch is Paya Rumput, where BN won by just 629 votes in 2021.
PAS is contesting the seat under the BN-PN arrangement, while PKR has fielded Anwar’s political secretary, Azman Abidin.
Amir Fareed said his team’s observations showed Umno and PAS campaigning closely together there, but the question remained whether BN supporters would turn out for a PAS candidate and whether Azman’s profile could help PKR attract Malay voters.
Bemban is another constituency to watch, with PN fielding a Wawasan candidate while Bersatu is contesting separately.
Amir Fareed said his team observed a strong Wawasan presence during the candidate’s walkabout, adding that the result could indicate how much support PN had retained since the 2022 general election.
For PH, the immediate tests include whether Amanah can retain Bukit Katil and DAP can defend Ayer Keroh, while PKR will be seeking to regain Machap Jaya and Kelebang.
In mixed constituencies such as DAP-held Ayer Keroh, where Malay voters make up roughly 42 per cent of the electorate, even relatively small shifts in support or turnout could influence the outcome, he said.
Amir Fareed said PH had room to make gains in a campaign that was less confrontational than the Johor state election, with Budget 2027 potentially giving it a boost.
However, Bersama, which has Rafizi playing a prominent campaign role, had been organising in Melaka even before the state assembly was dissolved and could draw support from the same pool of voters.
He also identified the controversy surrounding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest bid as a possible factor affecting PH supporters’ motivation to vote during the second week of campaigning.
Ultimately, Amir Fareed said the election would test whether voters were willing to transfer their support across newly formed political alliances, particularly when their preferred party was not contesting under its own banner.
“A voter can approve of the chief minister’s record and still hesitate to back his coalition partner’s candidate. Equally, a voter can be disappointed with PH nationally and still turn out for an assemblyman who has served the constituency well. In a quiet campaign, those decisions can be hard to see until polling day.
“In the closest seats, who stays home may matter as much as who switches sides,” he said.

Title: Deepavali traffic remains smooth nationwide, but return rush expected later today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Traffic flow on most major expressways nationwide remained smooth as of 8am today, but vehicle numbers are expected to increase later in the day as motorists return from the Deepavali and additional school holidays.
However, a Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) spokesperson said congestion was reported along the southbound stretch of the North-South Expressway (PLUS), from Yong Peng towards Ayer Hitam, following an accident.
“The accident, which occurred at Kilometre 82.3, involved a lorry and a car, but no fatalities were reported,” he told Bernama when contacted this morning.
The spokesperson said CCTV monitoring had yet to show a significant increase in traffic heading towards the Klang Valley, possibly due to the additional holiday today.
“Traffic volume is expected to increase between 10 am and 11 am as motorists return to the federal capital from the north, south and East Coast,” he added.
In view of the ongoing Northeast Monsoon, LLM advised highway users to maintain a safe following distance to reduce the risk of incidents involving sudden braking.
“Motorists are also advised to stop and rest at rest and service areas (R&Rs) if they feel tired or sleepy, while motorcyclists are encouraged to use the shelters provided by LLM and highway concessionaires during rainy conditions,” the spokesperson said.
For the latest traffic updates, the public can call LLM’s toll-free hotline at 1800-88-7752. — Bernama

Title: Remembering 2014’s great flood, Kelantan firefighters prepare for another big test
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 9 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM) is drawing on its experience in handling the massive 2014 floods to strengthen its preparedness for potential extreme disasters in the state, said its director, Farhan Sufyan Borhan.
He said the extraordinary scale of the 2014 floods, which affected vast areas of the state, posed significant challenges to rescue operations.
“Despite having a service continuity plan to ensure fire stations remain operational even when flooded, the scale of the 2014 disaster exceeded the state’s capacity to respond using its own resources.
“At the time, we were also affected by the floods, and our only option was to accept assistance from other states,” he told Bernama recently.
He said such situations underscored the importance of assistance from other states, particularly in terms of personnel and assets, to ensure rescue operations could continue when disasters exceeded the capacity of state agencies.
Farhan Sufyan said the proposed establishment of a regional forward base was among the measures being considered to strengthen response capabilities in the event of another major flood.
Meanwhile, he said the first one to six hours following a disaster were often the most challenging for rescue agencies, as operations had yet to be fully coordinated.
He said that the early stages of a disaster were often chaotic, with a surge in emergency calls requiring the deployment of personnel and assets to affected areas.
Farhan Sufyan said such situations were common in disaster management, particularly during floods, but advance planning and training could help minimise disruption during the initial response phase.
“Coordination among rescue agencies is also crucial to ensuring a swift response and avoiding duplication of efforts,” he said.
Farhan Sufyan also emphasised the need for continuous inter-agency cooperation, training and discussions to ensure all parties understood their respective roles during emergencies.
He added that such preparedness was crucial to ensuring more coordinated rescue operations, particularly during widespread flooding.
Yesterday, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued an alert-level continuous rain warning for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang and Sabah, as well as the whole of Terengganu, valid until Wednesday.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covered Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan.
Following the continuous rain warning, the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) warned of possible flooding in nine districts in Kelantan from today until Wednesday. — Bernama

Title: Penang police clarify abuse victim’s custody timeline after protection concerns raised
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 9 — Penang police said an 11-year-old girl allegedly sexually abused by her father was placed in her paternal grandmother’s temporary care on Oct 16, the day he was arrested and remanded, and handed to her mother on Oct 21, three days before his remand ended.
Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the girl’s school principal lodged a report with the Criminal Investigation Division of the Southwest District Police Headquarters at 11.15 am on Oct 16, and the suspect was arrested at about 5.30 pm that day and remanded until Oct 24.
“The girl was referred to the One Stop Crisis Centre (OSCC) at Penang Hospital on Oct 17 and remained in the paediatric ward until Oct 21, when the Southwest District Social Welfare Department (JKM) handed her to her biological mother,” he said in a statement tonight.
Lim said the girl was initially placed in her grandmother’s temporary care because her biological mother was in Singapore at the time.
He said the suspect was charged at the Balik Pulau Court on Oct 24 under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.
“The case is still being tried, with the next court mention scheduled for Nov 11, 2026,” he said and advised the public against speculating or spreading unverified information that could cause misunderstanding about the case.
The statement came following remarks by Berapit state assemblyman Heng Lee Lee in a news report last Thursday questioning the decision to allow the girl to return to a home allegedly shared with the suspect instead of being placed under immediate protection.
Heng urged the Social Welfare Department to adopt a more compassionate, flexible and responsive approach when handling vulnerable children, and called for seamless coordination among welfare officers, medical personnel and police. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi says child safety and cybersecurity must keep pace with AI
Article:
DOHA, Nov 9 — Malaysia has emphasised the need to strengthen cybersecurity and child online protection while ensuring the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said trust and safety were essential to enabling people to participate confidently in the digital economy, as technological advancements continued to reshape the way people lived and worked.
He said innovation must be accompanied by appropriate safeguards to protect users and build public confidence in digital technologies.
“The Declaration rightly puts a strong focus on cybersecurity, protecting children online, and ensuring that emerging technologies are developed and used responsibly.
“For Malaysia, innovation must go hand in hand with the right safeguards. This will give people the confidence to make full use of the opportunities that digital technologies offer,” he said at the Ministerial Roundtable held in conjunction with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26), here today.
Fahmi said Malaysia welcomed the draft Doha Ministerial Declaration, which outlined a comprehensive approach to addressing the opportunities and challenges of digital transformation.
He said the declaration reflected three priorities central to Malaysia’s national digital agenda, which were ensuring meaningful connectivity, promoting digital inclusion and fostering a safe and trusted digital environment.
He said meaningful connectivity must go beyond network coverage to ensure that telecommunications services remain affordable, reliable and resilient in supporting communities and economic activities.
Malaysia also welcomed the declaration’s emphasis on developing resilient and sustainable digital infrastructure to ensure the continuity of essential communications during emergencies and disruptions.
Fahmi said digital transformation must create opportunities for everyone regardless of geographical location or level of digital readiness.
He added that the Malaysian government remained focused on investing in digital skills and capacity building while supporting innovation to enable more people to benefit from the digital economy.
“As AI and other emerging technologies continue to develop, we must make sure that developing countries and underserved communities are not left behind.
“They should have the opportunity not only to use these technologies, but also to help shape them and benefit from the opportunities they create,” he said.
Fahmi also welcomed the declaration’s emphasis on international cooperation and acknowledged the ITU’s important role in expanding connectivity, developing technical standards and strengthening digital capacity.
He said Malaysia looked forward to working closely with the ITU and other member states to build a more connected and inclusive digital future while ensuring greater safety and equitable opportunities for all. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan braces for floods as nine districts face days of relentless rain
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 9 — Floods are expected in nine districts in Kelantan from Sunday until Wednesday (Nov 11), following a continuous rain warning issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
The National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) said the districts are Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Bachok, Machang, Pasir Mas, Pasir Puteh, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Jeli.
It said the preliminary flood forecast followed a Continuous Rain Warning (Alert) issued by MetMalaysia at 4.30pm today, with flood hotspots, low-lying areas and other flood-prone locations expected to be affected.
“In Kota Bharu, areas at risk are located within the Kelantan River Basin, while in Tumpat, they are within the Golok River Basin, covering Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua and Sungai Kelaboran,” it said in a statement tonight.
In Bachok, areas at risk are within the Kemasin River Basin, including Sungai Jelawat, Sungai Kemasin, Saliran PKS, Saliran KADA drainage and Sungai Bator.
The Semerak River Basin, covering Sungai Lubuk Nibong, Sungai Melor, Sungai Gunong and Sungai Semerak, is also at risk of flooding.
In Machang, areas at risk are within the Kelantan River Basin, including Sungai Kelantan, Sungai Kerawang, Sungai Kweng Hitam and watercourses in Machang town.
In Pasir Mas, flooding is forecast in the Golok River Basin, including Sungai Golok and Sungai Lemal, while in Pasir Puteh, the areas at risk are within the Semerak River Basin.
Areas at risk in Tanah Merah are within the Kelantan River Basin; Sungai Lebir and Sungai Galas, both part of the same basin in Kuala Krai; Sungai Pergau and Sungai Jeli in the Kelantan River Basin, as well as Sungai Lanas in the Golok River Basin in Jeli.
PRABN warned that flooding could occur earlier or later than the forecast period.
Residents, particularly those in flood-prone areas, are advised to remain vigilant and comply with instructions from the authorities.
The public can obtain the latest flood updates through the Public InfoBanjir website at https://publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my/. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan steps up social media push to win Melaka’s young and first-time voters
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Nov 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is stepping up efforts to win over young voters, particularly first-time voters, through more targeted campaigning, including the use of social media and face-to-face engagement, in the 16th Melaka state election.
Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said campaign strategies must adapt to changing communication trends, particularly when reaching out to young people who are more active on social media.
“While social media is an important campaign platform, traditional methods of engaging directly with voters must not be overlooked.
“We are dealing with people who need a personal touch. Every candidate must make every effort to meet voters in their respective constituencies,” he told reporters at the PH operations centre for the Machap Jaya state constituency in Batu Lesung here yesterday.
Muhammad Kamil said he had visited almost all the constituencies contested by PH in Melaka and would cover the remaining areas during the final five days of campaigning to garner voter support.
The political secretary to the Finance Minister said the party’s election machinery was also expected to intensify efforts to reach out to voters in the second week of campaigning to secure greater support for PH and boost voter turnout.
“We hope to maintain the positive momentum until polling day and intensify our efforts in the remaining campaign period to convince more voters to support us,” he said.
He said PH was focusing on 15 seats in its bid to secure enough seats to form the state government.
“God willing, our election machinery in all 15 constituencies will work hard to bring about change in Melaka,” he said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. —Bernama

Title: Brunei’s record 102kg syabu bust snares Malaysian suspect with two prior records
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — A Malaysian man arrested by Brunei authorities with more than 100 kilogrammes (kg) of suspected syabu at the Sungai Tujoh Control Post along the Brunei-Miri border on Oct 31 has two previous criminal records.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the 46-year-old suspect from Miri was believed to be on his way to Sabah when he was detained.
He said the department received information from Brunei’s Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) regarding the arrest of the man, along with about 100kg of suspected syabu valued at an estimated RM5 million.
“Information from Brunei’s NCB revealed that the man was arrested while entering the country from Miri, Sarawak, and was believed to have used the sultanate as a transit route before re-entering Malaysia,” he said when contacted here yesterday.
Hussein said preliminary investigations found the suspect was expected to travel through Kuala Belait, Seria, Tutong, and Bandar Seri Begawan before heading to Temburong across the Sultan Haji Omar Ali Saifuddien Bridge.
He said the man was believed to have planned to re-enter Sarawak through the Labu-Mengkalap route before proceeding to Sabah through Merapok-Sindumin.
“NCID will continue intelligence cooperation with Brunei’s NCB to identify the drug supply source and any possible links to syndicates in Malaysia,” he said.
Earlier, Brunei authorities reported the seizure of 102.19kg of syabu concealed in 100 tea packets at the Sungai Tujoh Control Post, estimated at BND2.8 million, marking the largest drug haul ever recorded at the border checkpoint.
Apart from the syabu, Brunei authorities also seized four Erimin 5 pills, cash comprising RM1,180, SG$10, BN$10, and 500 baht, two mobile phones, and a vehicle believed to have been used in the smuggling activity. — Bernama

Title: Watch the rivers: Flood threat looms over Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 9 — The National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage predicts that Kuantan, Pekan, and Rompin are likely to be hit by floods, especially in hotspot areas, low-lying regions, and at-risk locations from Sunday until Wednesday (Nov 11).
It said the forecast was following an alert-level continuous rain warning by the Meteorological Department at 4.30pm yesterday.
Among the locations predicted to be involved in Kuantan are areas within the Sungai Kuantan Basin, namely the Sungai Kuantan, Sungai Lembing, Sungai Kenau, Sungai Beserah, Sungai Belat and Sungai Soi.
“Also involved are the Sungai Cherating Basin (Sungai Cherating), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Lepar), and Sungai Penor Basin (Sungai Penor),” said the statement.
For the Pekan district, the areas involved are the Sungai Bebar Basin (Sungai Bebar), Sungai Miang Basin (Sungai Miang), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Pahang, Sungai Pahang Tua and Sungai Mentiga), while the Sungai Mercung Basin (Sungai Mercung) is also included.
In addition, in Rompin, it will involve areas in the Sungai Endau Basin (Sungai Endau and Sungai Anak Endau), Sungai Rompin Basin (Sungai Rompin, Sungai Pukin, Sungai Kepasing, Sungai Keratong, Sungai Jeram, Sungai Gayong, Sungai Chanis, Sungai Buan) as well as the Sungai Pontian Pahang Basin (Sungai Pontian Pahang).
“The predicted floods may occur earlier or later than expected. This warning is issued to enable all residents, especially in flood-prone areas, to be vigilant and comply with the instructions of the authorities or flood disaster management agencies,” according to the statement. — Bernama

Title: Monkeys on road leave two Terengganu police officers injured in patrol crash
Article:
HULU TERENGGANU, Nov 9 — Two police officers were injured after the patrol car they were in skidded and overturned while trying to avoid a group of monkeys at Kilometre 4, Jalan Simpang Bukit Kepah-Tapah, near Kampung Kepah, here yesterday.
Hulu Terengganu district police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said that in the incident at about 4.30pm, Lance Corporal Muhammad Amirul Hafiz Ahmad, 26, and Corporal Khairil Azlan Abdul Latif, 44, from the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Hulu Terengganu district police headquarters were carrying out traffic enforcement patrol duties in the Hulu Terengganu area.
He said the preliminary investigation found that the incident occurred when a police patrol car, driven by Muhammad Amirul Hafiz from the direction of Simpang Kepah towards Kuala Berang here, swerved to the right side of the road to avoid a pack of monkeys that suddenly appeared in the middle of the road.
“However, the vehicle skidded and overturned several times. The incident occurred at a bend and on a tarred and wet road surface after the rain,” he said when contacted today.
Sharudin said Muhammad Amirul Hafiz, who fractured his left arm, and his colleague Khairil Azlan, who experienced pain in his jaw, were sent to Hulu Terengganu Hospital for treatment. — Bernama

Title: Following Kraków attack, Malaysian embassy urges citizens to stay connected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The Malaysian Embassy in Warsaw is closely monitoring the situation in Kraków, Poland, following a shooting at the city’s Main Market Square on Saturday.
The embassy said it remained in contact with the Malaysian community in Kraków to ensure their safety.
“The Embassy encourages Malaysians in Poland to register their details with the Embassy,” it said in a Facebook post on Sunday.
The embassy also extended its condolences to the victims, their families and the people of Poland.
“Our thoughts and deepest condolences go out to the victims, their families, and the people of the Republic of Poland during this difficult period of national grief. Malaysia stands in solidarity with Poland against such senseless acts of violence,” it said.
Malaysians requiring emergency consular assistance may contact the embassy by telephone at +48 22 617 4413 during office hours or +48 660 627 360 (duty officer), or via email at mwwarsaw@kln.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Fighting scammers with AI and data: How Budget 2027 is sharpening Malaysia’s cybercrime defences
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — A message arrives offering an investment opportunity that sounds too good to miss.
The recipient is directed to a website or online group where supposed investors share screenshots of their profits and testimonials about how much they have earned.
Convinced that the opportunity is legitimate, the recipient is asked to register, transfer money into a bank account and act quickly before the offer closes.
By the time doubt sets in, the money may already be gone.
Such scams are among the online threats that can catch people off guard, often relying on convincing messages, fabricated testimonials and pressure to make quick decisions.
Budget 2027 introduces three initiatives aimed at addressing online threats: an artificial intelligence (AI) application developed by the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC), an upgrade to the police’s system for detecting child exploitation, and an expanded internet safety campaign in schools.
How will these initiatives help protect Malaysians from online threats?
A new AI application to check before you pay
Under Budget 2027, the NSRC will develop an AI application that allows users to check suspicious phone numbers, bank accounts and links before making a transaction.
The initiative is intended to help Malaysians identify potential scams before transferring money or clicking on potentially harmful links.
In a statement published by the National Security Council on October 12, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the application would help the public carry out preliminary checks and reduce their risk of falling victim to digital fraud.
The proposed application will add another public-facing tool to Malaysia’s existing anti-scam efforts.
The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) already operates Semak Mule, which allows the public to check whether bank accounts, telephone numbers and company names have been associated with reported commercial crimes.
The NSRC also has an existing National Fraud Portal (NFP), which helps authorities and financial institutions speed up fund tracking and the detection of mule accounts through data integration and predictive analytics.
In February 2026, Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the centre received 19,438 online scam-related calls in January, with RM2.408 billion in victims’ funds successfully frozen before they could be siphoned off.
Of that amount, RM321.3 million, or 13 per cent, was returned to victims.
How can you check whether a phone number or bank account is linked to a scam?
The application is intended to help users identify potential risks, although its results should not be treated as a guarantee that a transaction is safe.
There are also existing tools that can help consumers check for potential scams and complement the proposed NSRC application, but they perform different checks.
Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) Financial Consumer Alert List identifies entities or schemes that may have been wrongly represented as licensed or regulated, while the Securities Commission (SC) Malaysia’s Investor Alert List flags unauthorised entities and individuals.
The BNM and SC tools help consumers check whether a financial institution, investment company or scheme has been flagged by the regulators.
However, both regulators caution that their lists are not exhaustive, meaning that an entity or scheme not appearing on the lists is not necessarily legitimate.
The government has also advised that anyone who has fallen victim to a financial scam should immediately contact their bank or the NSRC through its 997 hotline.
BNM also advises victims to lodge a police report.
Detecting online crimes against children
Budget 2027 also provides for the PDRM’s D11 division to enhance the Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children system with advanced analytics capabilities.
The upgrade aims to strengthen police capabilities in identifying perpetrators and uncovering networks involved in child sexual exploitation.
In a statement following the Budget announcement on October 9, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail welcomed the initiative, saying the measures could strengthen the detection of online scams and improve protection for children against sexual exploitation.
How will the Safe Internet Campaign protect children?
Alongside the police system upgrade, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will intensify the implementation of its Safe Internet Campaign in all schools, with a focus on tackling cyberbullying and child exploitation.
The campaign aims to raise awareness of online risks among pupils and encourage safer internet use, particularly as children face harmful behaviour and exploitation on digital platforms.
How do the three initiatives work together?
The three measures announced under Budget 2027 address different aspects of online safety.
Together, these initiatives combine public-facing scam checks, stronger investigative capabilities and online safety education as part of the government’s efforts to tackle digital crime.

Title: BN-Perikatan cooperation may not translate into full voter support, says Melaka Pakatan chairman
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 16th Melaka state election does not guarantee a full transfer of votes between their supporters, despite the apparent advantage of such an arrangement on paper.
State Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari said supporters of the two coalitions might not necessarily embrace the cooperation, while new voters could also influence the election outcome.
He said some voters had chosen PN in previous elections because they did not want to support BN, and the cooperation could therefore affect their existing support base.
“The same applies to BN. For example, based on the Negeri Sembilan state election results, the highest vote transfer rate recorded was 70 per cent.
“This means that the remaining 30 per cent of BN votes might not go to PN. In Melaka, however, the rate could be 60 or even 50 per cent, depending on how supporters of both coalitions respond to the cooperation,” he said after attending a Ziarah Kasih programme at Rumah Awam Bukit Beruang here today.
Adly was responding to a question about his confidence in retaining the Bukit Katil seat in the state election.
Elaborating further, the former Melaka chief minister said the nearly 4,000 new voters in Bukit Katil could also influence voting patterns, as most had no strong allegiance to any political party.
He said Bukit Katil was a mixed constituency, with Malays accounting for about 65 per cent of voters, followed by Chinese (29 per cent) and Indians (five per cent).
He added that playing on racial and religious sentiments to win votes did not guarantee support from voters whose loyalties were divided among several political parties.
“In the previous state election, Malay support for PH exceeded 27 per cent, and we will try to increase that figure in this election,” he said.
He said his eight-year track record as the Bukit Katil assemblyman was also an advantage in his bid to secure a third term.
Adly is facing Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif of PN, Dr Aliza Che Amran (Parti Bersama Malaysia) and Abu Bakar Sabudin (Independent) in a four-cornered contest for the seat.
In the previous state election, Adly retained the seat with a majority of 1,057 votes.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain triggers flash floods in Taman Sri Muda, no displacement reported
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — No evacuations have been carried out in Taman Sri Muda, Section 25 here following flash floods triggered by heavy rain this afternoon, which were also captured in videos circulating on social media.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a similar incident was also detected in Kampung Baru Hicom, Section 26 during the department’s monitoring around Shah Alam.
“Water has risen at several locations, spilling onto roads due to overflowing drains. However, no evacuations have been carried out in the affected areas. The latest situation shows that the rain has stopped, although the weather remains cloudy,” he said in a statement today.
He said monitoring was also being carried out in other high-risk areas, including Jalan Kebun Bunga in Section 22, Section 13 and Jalan Kebun.
Earlier, social media users shared updates on flash floods following heavy rain between 3 pm and 5 pm today.
The posts included images and videos of areas around Taman Sri Muda and a shopping mall in Bukit Tinggi, Klang, showing rising water levels following the heavy rain. — Bernama

Title: Police secure remand of nine suspects over deadly Sibu brawl
Article:
SIBU, Nov 8 — Nine suspects have been remanded for seven days until Nov 15 to assist in the investigation into the death of a 19-year-old male believed to have been stabbed during a brawl here yesterday.
Sibu District Police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspects, aged between 16 and 42, were brought to court at 7.15 am today for the remand application.
He said a post-mortem examination completed today revealed that the victim died of chest injuries.
“The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” he said.
The Sibu District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Department launched an operation to track down those believed to be involved after receiving a report at about 2 am yesterday.
All the suspects were rounded up at several locations around Sibu between 10 am and 4 pm yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Second 5G network achieves 90pc coverage ahead of schedule, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA, Nov 8 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil highlighted Malaysia’s progress in expanding its 5G network at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026, with the country’s second 5G network achieving 90 per cent coverage in October this year, nine months ahead of schedule.
He said the achievement marked significant progress in Malaysia’s transition towards a dual 5G network model aimed at strengthening competition, encouraging investment and improving telecommunications service quality.
Fahmi said Malaysia had also made significant investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) since 2020.
“As of July 2026, approximately 10.12 million premises had been passed by fibre, significantly improving access to high-speed broadband services,” he said at the Digital Leadership Forum Ministerial Panel held in conjunction with MWC Doha 2026 here today.
Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial progress in 5G deployment, with the second network achieving 90 per cent coverage nine months ahead of schedule.
He said the development reflected the country’s efforts to establish a competitive and sustainable telecommunications ecosystem while ensuring that consumers benefited from improved service quality.
However, Fahmi stressed that Malaysia’s digital infrastructure development was not solely focused on expanding network coverage, as service quality, affordability and resilience were equally important.
He said these elements must be addressed together to ensure that digital connectivity delivered meaningful benefits to the people.
“Through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, or MCMC, we continue to promote infrastructure sharing and efficient network deployment, while addressing connectivity gaps in underserved communities,” he said.
Fahmi said the Universal Service Provision (USP) framework also played an important role in extending telecommunications services to areas where commercial investment alone might not be viable.
He said the approach enabled Malaysia to balance infrastructure investment with the need to ensure that telecommunications services remained accessible and affordable.
“For Malaysia, a successful network model is one that combines strong infrastructure, sustainable investment, effective regulation and meaningful access for all,” he added.
Fahmi is currently in Doha to lead the Malaysian delegation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26), which runs from Nov 6 to 11.
His working visit to Doha also carries the important mission of securing Malaysia’s re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
He is accompanied by Communications Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Telecommunications Infrastructure) Mano Verabathran.
The Malaysian delegation also comprises representatives from the MCMC and local telecommunications industry players, including Telekom Malaysia (TM), CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia to leverage AI and satellite networks for disaster preparedness
Article:
DOHA, Nov 8 — Malaysia sees significant opportunities to leverage satellite connectivity and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience, said Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil.
Speaking at the Digital Leadership Forum Ministerial Panel held in conjunction with Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026 here today, he said emerging technologies could complement conventional telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in remote and disaster-affected areas where alternative connectivity solutions might be required.
He said Malaysia also saw potential in integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to strengthen communications resilience during emergencies.
“Looking ahead, Malaysia sees opportunities to further leverage emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, satellite connectivity and integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks, to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience.
“These technologies can complement conventional infrastructure, particularly in remote or disaster-affected areas where alternative connectivity solutions may be required,” he said.
Fahmi said Malaysia was placing greater emphasis on strengthening emergency telecommunications capabilities to ensure essential communications remained available when conventional networks were disrupted.
He said reliable connectivity was crucial during disasters as it enabled emergency response teams to coordinate rescue operations and affected communities to access essential information.
“During a disaster, connectivity is not merely a convenience. It can be the difference between receiving timely assistance and being left isolated,” he said.
To address these challenges, Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had developed MCMC PRIME, a mobile radio and internet communications system designed to support connectivity when conventional telecommunications networks are disrupted..
He said the system provided an alternative means of communication during emergencies and supported coordination among response teams while maintaining access to essential information.
He said the initiative was particularly relevant during severe flooding when damaged telecommunications infrastructure or disrupted electricity supply could affect conventional mobile networks.
Fahmi said Malaysia’s approach also emphasised close coordination between MCMC and telecommunications operators, as well as the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) and other relevant authorities.
He said such cooperation was essential to support disaster preparedness and identify affected network infrastructure while coordinating restoration efforts and facilitating communications for emergency responders and affected communities.
He also stressed the importance of timely public warnings and reliable access to official information to enable communities to take appropriate precautionary measures during emergencies.
“Network resilience is not simply about preventing infrastructure failure. It is about ensuring that essential communications can continue, or be restored as quickly as possible, when lives and public safety are at stake,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Nations must decide own digital future, not be dictated to, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA, Nov 8— Malaysia has called for greater respect for national sovereignty in shaping telecommunications policies, warning against a form of “technology colonialism” in which technologically advanced nations dictate how other countries develop and deploy their digital infrastructure.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said every nation must retain the freedom to determine its own technological direction, particularly as geopolitical rivalries and competing technology ecosystems increasingly influence global telecommunications development.
“There should not be a case of a kind of technology colonialism where if you are the first, then you dictate to others what you should or shouldn’t do, what you can or cannot do.
“Nations are sovereign and should be able to decide their own domestic policy,” he said during a ministerial panel discussion at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026 here today.
Fahmi said Malaysia’s experience in rolling out its 5G network demonstrated the importance of maintaining policy independence while navigating complex geopolitical and diplomatic considerations.
He noted that Malaysia initially adopted a single wholesale network model for its 5G deployment despite recommendations against such an approach by GSMA Intelligence, before subsequently transitioning to a dual-network model.
“Malaysia is unique because we did what GSMA Intelligence said not to do: roll out 5G using a single wholesale network. But we did it anyway, and I was the minister in charge of transitioning it into a dual-network model,” he said.
Fahmi described the transition as a challenging undertaking that required Malaysia to navigate diplomatic sensitivities while balancing domestic priorities against international technological standards.
He stressed that discussions on digital sovereignty should extend beyond technological self-reliance to encompass the broader principle of national sovereignty.
The minister also said an increasingly multipolar global environment demands greater dialogue and engagement among countries to find common ground rather than deepen divisions.
“In this increasingly multipolar age, we need to have more conversations, more engagements, and find meeting points rather than things that split us apart,” he added.
Fahmi said the principle of interoperability, which enables different telecommunications networks and technologies to function together, would face significant tests as countries pursued their respective digital strategies.
He pointed out that ASEAN’s consensus-based approach presents its own unique dynamics, given the absence of a central parliament and the bloc’s strong emphasis on respecting member states’ national sovereignty.
As such, he said, building trust and achieving interoperability requires countries to look beyond their national borders and bolster international cooperation.
Fahmi also highlighted the need to assist emerging nations in bridging digital divides, particularly as the telecommunications sector prepares for quantum migration and quantum-safe communications.
He noted that greater focus should be placed on driving the practical adoption of existing networks before the industry shifts its attention entirely to sixth-generation (6G) technologies.
“Before we talk about 6G, we have to look at who is actually using 5G or 5G-Advanced - that remains a key challenge we are actively addressing in Malaysia,” he said.
Despite the hurdles, Fahmi expressed confidence that international collaboration could spur innovative breakthroughs, particularly from nations not traditionally viewed as global technology leaders.
“There are many challenges, but there are also many opportunities for us to discover solutions together, and sometimes you might find those solutions in the unlikeliest of countries,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police raid unlicensed KL entertainment outlet, detain 195 underage patrons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Police detained 195 underage teenagers and a premises manager in a raid on an unlicensed entertainment outlet in the capital after midnight last night.
Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the teenagers detained in the operation, conducted at about 12.30 am, comprised 93 local males, 61 local females, 16 foreign males and 25 foreign females.
He said 16 outlet workers and 219 other patrons were also checked.
He said investigations found that the entertainment outlet was operating without a licence and allowing underage patrons to enter.
“The premises manager is being investigated under Section 29(2) of the Entertainment (Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur) Regulations 1993 for allowing underage patrons into the entertainment premises.
“All those detained, aged between 18 and 64, were taken to the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters for summonses, documentation and further investigation,” he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Azwan said checks found that none of the individuals inspected had any outstanding criminal records, while preliminary urine screening found an adult male patron positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
He said the operation reflected Kuala Lumpur Police’s commitment to ensuring public safety and well-being.
“Enforcement action will continue to be intensified to curb any illegal activities,” he said.
He also urged members of the public with information on criminal activities to channel it through the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522 / 03-2146 0585, the Dang Wangi District Police Control Centre at 03-2600 2222 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidate for Paya Rumput aims to ease voting process with personalised polling slips
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Paya Rumput state constituency Datuk Azman Abidin has introduced an initiative to help voters check their polling locations and channels ahead of the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14.
Azman, popularly known as Tok Man, said he and his campaign team would assist voters in checking their polling details while campaigning, with the results printed on small slips and handed to them for reference.
He said the initiative used electoral roll data provided by the Election Commission (EC) to candidates, with the information entered into a system specially developed by PH to facilitate the checking and printing of voter slips.
“Under this initiative, campaign workers only need to enter a voter’s identity card number to retrieve information on their polling location, including the school and assigned polling channel,” he told reporters after attending a courtesy visit and meet-and-greet programme with the Paya Rumput state constituency campaign machinery today.
Also present at the programme, held at the PH Main Operations Room in Krubong here, was PKR Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, who is also Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament.
Azman, who is also the Prime Minister’s Political Secretary, said the idea for the initiative came about after he found that many voters he met during the campaign period could not remember their respective polling centres and channels.
“With this slip, which is more practical than the standard A4-sized printout used previously, voters can not only check their polling details but also keep it in their wallets or pockets for reference again on polling day,” he said.
On the campaign’s progress as it enters its final week, Azman said he would make full use of the remaining time to reach as many residents of the Paya Rumput constituency as possible.
“We will try to cover all areas and reach out to everyone in Paya Rumput, Insha-Allah. The campaign has been going well, in an orderly and peaceful manner. I hope it will remain so until polling day,” he said.
The 16th Melaka State Election will see a three-cornered contest in Paya Rumput between Azman, Rafie Ahmad of Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
The EC has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026
. — Bernama

Title: Penang Sentral offers round-the-clock waiting space for travellers, says Zairil
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Nov 8 — Penang Sentral, an integrated transport hub and major commercial development, provides a 24-hour waiting area on Level 1 at its stage bus platform, equipped with basic facilities for passengers.
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the facility was intended for passengers waiting for buses or their next connecting transport service.
He said Penang Sentral was operated by Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and not the state government, adding that the waiting area was not meant to serve as accommodation or an overnight stay facility.
“MRCB also explained that public access to the terminal is restricted to Level 1 after 1 am, with visitors not allowed to wait or remain in other areas, including the commercial sections and the Urban Transformation Centre (UTC), which are closed for security and operational reasons,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
He was commenting on a social media post alleging that a passenger had been asked to leave the terminal by security guards after arriving at about 1 am.
The passenger claimed he had been waiting for a ferry to George Town, with his hotel check-in scheduled only for 3 pm the following day.
Feedback from members of the public has also highlighted the need for a dedicated waiting space, particularly for passengers arriving on late-night or early-morning express buses.
University student Hana Nurdira Muhammad Haikal, 20, who studies in Kelantan and frequently returns to Penang during semester breaks, said she often arrived at Penang Sentral early in the morning with her friends, adding that the differing needs of passengers should be taken into consideration.
“I believe MRCB could consider providing a dedicated waiting area for passengers arriving late at night or with early-morning travel schedules. It does not necessarily have to offer accommodation, but should at least have sufficient seating and accessible toilets,” she said.
Kuala Lumpur-based bank officer Shahril Reza Ibrahim, 35, who regularly travels by express bus, said such facilities were important for long-distance passengers, especially those continuing their journeys by ferry.
“MRCB may have its reasons in terms of security and operational control, but from the perspective of user experience, there are still some shortcomings that need to be addressed. As a frequent express bus passenger, I often use Terminal Bersepadu Selatan, which is equipped with a waiting area,” he said.
Penang Sentral serves as an integrated transport hub connecting ferry services, KTM train services, express buses and Rapid Penang buses, with the Mutiara Line LRT also planned to serve the area.
Meanwhile, UTC Seberang Perai, which occupies the third and fourth floors of the terminal and spans more than 60,000 square feet, houses nine government departments, including the Immigration Department and the National Registration Department. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of prolonged rain in four states until Wednesday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of continuous rain at the alert level for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang, Sabah and Terengganu, until Wednesday.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan.
In Pahang, the areas affected are Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, while the warning covers the whole of Terengganu.
In Sabah, continuous rain is forecast from tomorrow until Wednesday in Kudat and Sandakan, covering Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan.
The public can obtain the latest weather information through MetMalaysia’s official website and social media platforms, as well as its myCuaca mobile application.
For further enquiries, the public can contact the MetMalaysia hotline at 1-300-22-1638. — Bernama

Title: Melaka plans five-year push to transform Kota Laksamana into state capital
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 —Kota Laksamana has the potential to become the new state capital of Melaka due to rapid development that can catalyse economic growth and transform the state's landscape, says Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said the state government has formulated a five-year development plan for the area and will work alongside the private sector to realise that potential.
"The plans are in place, but we have yet to integrate them because these concessions were awarded to private companies undertaking projects under the Private Finance Initiative (PFI). This is beyond our control as they have acquired the land.
"However, the state government will coordinate with the private sector, provide necessary support and reduce bureaucracy to accelerate economic activity in Kota Laksamana," he told reporters when met at Jalan Hang Tuah here today.
Ab Rauf said the development plan also encompasses areas under the Straits of Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone (SM-WEZ), covering commercial, residential, healthcare and tourism sectors.
"I appeal to the people to join me in developing Melaka and breathing new life into Kota Laksamana so that it can serve as the new state capital," he said.
Commenting on preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, Ab Rauf said the state government has stepped up disaster preparedness, including identifying 102 flood hotspots across the state.
He said the locations were identified based on records of floods recurring at least three times within three years.
"Preparedness measures include round-the-clock flood monitoring across six major river basins, alongside continuous recording of rainfall data and river water levels.
"The early warning system has also been enhanced with the installation of 14 flood warning sirens and 10 surveillance cameras at strategic locations across Melaka," he added.
Ab Rauf said flood mitigation assets have also been readied, comprising 21 water control gates, 21 pump houses and 14 portable emergency pumps that can be mobilised to critical areas, in addition to monitoring 105 flood retention ponds.
He added that 447 small-scale works worth RM43.8 million have been carried out this year to bolster flood management infrastructure and mitigate disaster risks.
He also advised residents, particularly in coastal areas, to remain vigilant as the high-tide phenomenon expected until Nov 17 could cause flash floods in low-lying areas.
"The state government will continue to issue early alerts and advisories through the Melaka State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) to ensure effective emergency response," he said. — Bernama

Title: BN-Pakatan relationship unaffected by Najib pardon issue, says Zahid
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — Differences in political views and positions among parties in the Unity Government have not affected the smooth administration of the government, said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the working relationship between BN and Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the government remained good, with the administration of ministries and Cabinet meetings proceeding smoothly and professionally.
“There are no problems in terms of our relationship. We manage the ministries and hold Cabinet meetings every week. Government affairs and administration are carried out professionally, and there have never been any differences of opinion or disputes over the past four years,” he told Malaysian media here at a press conference to wrap up his four-day working visit to Türkiye, which ended today.
Ahmad Zahid was asked to comment on whether the issue of a conditional pardon for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak could affect relations between BN and PH in the Unity Government.
Elaborating,  the Deputy Prime Minister said differences in political approaches and positions among parties should be addressed maturely, particularly when political situations differ at the federal and state levels.
He cited the previous Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, as well as the ongoing Melaka state election campaign, which highlighted differences in political approaches at the state level despite BN and PH working together in the federal government.
“In my view, political maturity in Malaysia is now at an almost optimum level, and although there are different political moves and approaches, insya-Allah, these will not affect the country’s political stability,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Flood-prone areas under close watch as wet weather looms in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 8 — The Penang Fire and Rescue Department has stepped up patrols and monitoring in flash flood-prone areas throughout the state following forecasts of rain and thunderstorms until Tuesday.
Its director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said the measures were aimed at ensuring that personnel remained at optimal readiness to deal with any possible disasters during the Northeast Monsoon.
“Based on weather forecasts issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), rain and thunderstorms are expected in several areas of Penang from today until Nov 10, with the three-day forecast indicating a relatively frequent rainfall pattern, particularly in the afternoons and evenings,” he told Bernama today.
He said today’s forecast indicated rain in several areas in the morning, followed by thunderstorms in most areas in the afternoon and rain in most places at night.
He said tomorrow’s weather was expected to be wetter, with rain in most areas in the morning and thunderstorms forecast across the state in the afternoon, followed by rain in most places at night.
Mohamad Shoki said that on Tuesday, rain was forecast in several coastal areas in the morning, while conditions were expected to ease slightly in the afternoon and evening, although thunderstorms and rain were still forecast in some areas.
He said that despite the expected wet weather, MetMalaysia had informed that no Level 1 (Alert) Continuous Rain Warning had been issued for Penang so far.
“Following the forecast, the Operations Division of the Penang Fire and Rescue Department advises the public to remain alert to the latest weather warnings issued by the authorities.
“Residents, particularly those living in low-lying and flash flood-prone areas, are urged to avoid travelling along high-risk routes during thunderstorms. Anyone requiring emergency assistance or evacuation is advised to immediately call the 24-hour emergency hotline at 999,” he said, adding that the department was fully prepared to deal with any possible disasters throughout the monsoon period to safeguard lives and public property.
He also shared that monitoring operations involving seven Fire and Rescue Stations on the island and in Seberang Perai, including low-lying settlements and major river basins, began last night and that river levels and water flow at all locations inspected remained under control.
Among the locations monitored in Seberang Perai were Sungai Jawi, Sungai Duri, Sungai Junjong and Sungai Kechil, as well as Kampung Sethu, Kampung Sepulau, Kampung Sanglang and Kampung Valdor, Mohamad Shoki added.
“Monitoring was also conducted at Lahar Yooi, Labuh Banting, Ayer Itam, Jalan Permatang Rawa, Jalan Betik and Jalan Soo Ban Kheang in Bukit Mertajam. On the island, patrols focused on areas around Teluk Kumbar and Balik Pulau, as well as several other hotspots under the supervision of the Lebuh Pantai Fire and Rescue Station,” he said.
He said patrols would continue to enable the Fire and Rescue Department to issue early warnings to residents should there be any sudden changes in water levels. — Bernama

Title: Was a BN convoy given priority? Two-car collision at Melaka traffic lights sparks questions
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — A Threads video is raising questions over whether traffic police gave a Barisan Nasional (BN) convoy priority at the time of a two-car accident at a junction on the Alor Gajah-Melaka Tengah-Jasin (AMJ) highway.
The video from a dashboard camera showed a car turning right at the traffic lights junction while another car was travelling straight when they collided, veering into the front vehicles on a third lane.
The video, posted by Threads user @alfshrf, was shared with claims that traffic police had held back road users to let the convoy through.
On social media, someone remarked that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers and asked what had earned the group priority on the road.
It noted that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers, and asked what had earned the group priority on the road.
If the priority was tied to an individual’s security, the post asked who that person was, in what capacity, and whether it extended to the whole convoy.
It said the accident should be investigated, asking whether there had been confusion over instructions and how movement from each direction was controlled.
The post added that video footage alone did not settle who was at fault.
It called on the police to explain how traffic was managed at the time.
It also said questions about the convoy itself should be answered by Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh and the party, since the vehicles carried the identity of the coalition he leads in the state.
Among the questions it asked were who led the convoy, where it was heading, and on what basis other road users were stopped for it.
The post also voiced concern that party convoys appeared to receive treatment ordinary motorists do not, even as campaigning for the state election was still under way.
Malay Mail
could not independently verify the video or the claims accompanying it, and no statement from the police, BN or Ab Rauf was immediately available.

Title: AKPS detains 28-tonne buffalo meat shipment over import document irregularities
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) at Port Klang seized a consignment of buffalo meat, valued at RM413,728 and imported from India, at Port Klang on Friday (Nov 6).
Port Klang AKPS commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said an inspection conducted by enforcement officers at 10.40am detected discrepancies between the halal certificate documents submitted and the information declared in the import permit.
“The documents were found to contain information that did not correspond with the declaration. Following this, the entire consignment weighing 27,984 kilogrammes (kg) was seized for further investigation,” he said in a statement posted on the Port Klang AKPS Facebook page today.
Nik Ezanee said the goods would be handed over to the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) for further action, with the case being investigated under the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011 (Act 728).
He also reaffirmed AKPS’ commitment to intensifying enforcement efforts and strengthening controls at the country’s entry points to combat non-compliance, document manipulation and abuse of import procedures. — Bernama

Title: Perak MMEA seizes vessel, probes unauthorised anchoring and reporting lapses
Article:
IPOH, Nov 8 —The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Perak detained a cargo vessel suspected of violating the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952, about 4.3 nautical miles southwest of Pulau Jarak, near Lumut, yesterday.
Its director, Maritime Captain Zainudin Mohd Zuki, said the Lumut Maritime Surveillance System radar detected the Gambian-registered vessel, prompting the Perak Maritime Headquarters Operations Centre to alert enforcement teams for inspection.
He said the vessel had 21 crew members, including 11 Pakistanis, eight Iranians and two Indonesians.
“The vessel was suspected of two offences under the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952: anchoring without authorisation from the Director of Marine Malaysia and failing to report its arrival in Malaysian waters,” he said in a statement today.
Zainudin said the crew and chief engineer were taken to the Perak Maritime Headquarters to assist in the investigation, while the vessel’s documents were seized for further action. — Bernama

Title: Melaka lacks a real capital, says Ab Rauf, who wants Kota Laksamana to be it
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) wants to turn Kota Laksamana into Melaka’s state capital if it wins the seat in the coming state election, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said.
He said the idea is part of a plan for a new economic corridor that would reshape the area over the next five years, Berita Harian reported today.
“God willing, I am targeting Kota Laksamana to become the capital of Melaka,” he said at a campaign event at BN’s Kota Laksamana operations room here, attended by MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong and BN candidate Melvin Chua Kew Wei.
He asked who could say where Melaka’s capital is today, then answered that there is none.
“So if we win Kota Laksamana, we will give the people of Kota Laksamana a centre that will become Melaka’s state capital,” he said.
Ab Rauf, who is also acting chief minister, said the corridor would include a medical hub, along with tourism and commercial projects, building on Encore Melaka, Oriental Specialist Hospital and a new shopping centre in Klebang.
He said the work would be done in stages, with the first five years laying the groundwork.
Ab Rauf also said a BN win in Kota Laksamana was not out of reach, expressing confidence that Melvin could spring a surprise.
“Our target is Kota Laksamana, and I think this time, this year, this month, this term, it is not impossible for Melvin to become the assemblyman.
“Time and circumstances call for change, and if we stay where we are, it will be hard to change,” he said.
He said the state government would help provide facilities and cut red tape to speed up development in the area.
Chua faces a three-cornered fight against Pakatan Harapan’s Low Chee Leong of DAP and Parti Bersama Malaysia’s Ethan Lim Zhi Hao.
Low defended the seat in the 2021 election with a majority of 11,494 votes.
Early voting for the 16th Melaka state election is on Tuesday, with polling day this Saturday.

Title: Fake cops cheat retiree of RM179,490 in money laundering scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 —A 73-year-old retiree lost RM179,490 after falling victim to a Macau scam involving fraudsters posing as police officers and accusing him of money laundering and drug trafficking.
Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the victim was initially contacted by two unidentified individuals claiming to be police officers, who instructed him to surrender his bank cards, cash and jewellery for investigation purposes.
He said the victim, who panicked, later agreed to meet the suspects at an apartment in Sri Petaling on Sept 8 to hand over the money and valuables as instructed.
“The total losses amounted to RM179,490, involving cash handed over, gold purchases and transfers to three third-party bank accounts,” he said when contacted today.
Hoo said the victim lodged a police report after realising he had been cheated.
Police were checking information with telecommunications companies and reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage to assist investigations under Section 420 of the Penal Code, he added. — Bernama
